code: # unnumbered: ships no output; the table in the commented Shape B is a diagnostic only # ---- Shape A: no interval censoring ----------------------------------------- # SAS `time <t>; event <e>;` maps straight onto Surv(time, status). Nothing # below needs the interval machinery and `objective = "sas"` does not apply. # Demo: your time and status variables. resp <- data.frame(time   = as.numeric(d[[TIME]]),                    status = as.numeric(d[[EVENT]])) stopifnot(all(resp$status %in% c(0, 1)), !anyNA(resp$time))  # ---- Shape B: interval-censored --------------------------------------------- # Demo: delete Shape A above and uncomment this, from SAS's #   time <upper>; icensor <flag>=<lower>; # Expressed as Surv(type = "interval2"): an exact event is (t, t), a # right-censored row is (t, NA), an interval-censored row is (lo, hi). # # ⚠️ Do NOT pass the bounds through time_lower/time_upper. time_lower is an # ENTRY time for left truncation, not an interval bound, and using it that way # fits a different model without complaining. # # status_sas <- ifelse(!is.na(d$<flag>) & d$<flag> == 1, 2, #               ifelse(d$<event> == 1, 1, 0)) # lo   <- ifelse(status_sas == 2, d$<lower>, d$<upper>) # hi   <- ifelse(status_sas == 0, NA,        d$<upper>) # resp <- data.frame(lo = lo, hi = hi) # knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(`SAS status` = status_sas)))  # ONE source of truth for the response formula. Every hazard() call below uses # it, so the Shape A / Shape B choice above is made once and only once. Three # literal formulas would be three chances to edit two of them -- and while the # mismatched call usually errors on a missing column, an author who edits all # three INCONSISTENTLY gets no such warning. surv_formula <- if (all(c("lo", "hi") %in% names(resp))) {   Surv(lo, hi, type = "interval2") ~ 1 } else {   Surv(time, status) ~ 1 } # The response build is the step that fails SILENTLY. Get it wrong -- mark an # interval-censored death as right-censored at its upper bound, the opposite # claim -- and the fit still converges, on a number that is simply wrong. # # So the two event counts are compared here rather than left for the reader to # compare. A WARNING, not a stop: the cohort gate is defined on its own # variables, and a study where those legitimately differ from the fitted pair # should say so here rather than be blocked. n_fitted <- if ("status" %in% names(resp)) {   sum(resp$status == 1, na.rm = TRUE) } else {   sum(!is.na(resp$hi), na.rm = TRUE) } knitr::kable(data.frame(   source = c("cohort gate", "response as built"),   n_events = c(cc$n_events, n_fitted) )) if (!identical(as.integer(n_fitted), as.integer(cc$n_events))) {   warning("The response carries ", n_fitted, " events but the cohort gate ",           "counted ", cc$n_events, ". Reconcile before reading the fit.",           call. = FALSE) } # The objective is a log-likelihood. A positive one is impossible: it signals a # response that was mis-specified rather than a fit. Assert it, instead of # reporting a plateau as a result. check_fit <- function(f, label) {   o <- f$fit$objective   if (!is.finite(o) || o > 0) {     stop(label, ": objective is ", o, ", which is not a log-likelihood.",          call. = FALSE)   }   invisible(f) }

code: # No `condition` in control: SAS's CONDITION= option has no equivalent in # hazard(), which ignores the element with a warning in the report. The fit # reports the conditioning of its Hessian afterwards instead, as rcond below. fit_det <- hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                   phases = phases, theta = theta0, fit = TRUE,                   control = list(conserve = TRUE,                                  n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)) check_fit(fit_det, "deterministic") summary(fit_det) Multiphase hazard model (2 phases)   observations: 725    predictors:   0    dist:         multiphase    phase 1:      early - cdf (early risk)   phase 2:      late - g3 (late risk)   engine:       native-r-m2    converged:    TRUE    gradient:     relative 3.33e-06 (SAS/C requires <= 6.06e-06; met)   log-lik:      -1503.29    Not done in this run: none   evaluations: fn=6, gr=1  Coefficients (internal scale):    Phase: early (cdf)                estimate std_error     z_stat      p_value   log_mu     -3.5475335 0.6503541 -5.4547723 4.903564e-08   log_t_half -5.4139983 2.4642214 -2.1970421 2.801744e-02   nu          2.6936482 2.3449537  1.1486999 2.506797e-01   m          -0.2197872 0.4695841 -0.4680465 6.397513e-01    Phase: late (g3)             estimate  std_error    z_stat      p_value   log_mu  -2.5663963 0.17126255 -14.98516 9.180758e-51   log_tau  0.0000000         NA        NA           NA   gamma    1.0000000         NA        NA           NA   alpha    1.0000000         NA        NA           NA   eta      0.8800072 0.05681755  15.48830 4.161509e-54 # There is no logLik() method for class "hazard": the log-likelihood is # fit$fit$objective. # # rcond and pd are read OFF THE FIT rather than recomputed from vcov(): vcov() # includes every FIXED parameter as an all-NA row and column, and rcond() # cannot take an NA matrix. The fit's own values are computed on the free # parameters, which is also what SAS's condition number refers to. # # A multiphase fit reports how many times the optimizer evaluated the function # and its gradient, not an iteration count. Each value is read through .one(), # so a field a fit does not carry shows as "not reported" rather than changing # the number of rows and stopping the render. .one <- function(x, ...) if (length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x)) format(x, ...) else "not reported" knitr::kable(data.frame(   quantity = c("log-likelihood", "converged", "function evaluations", "gradient evaluations", "rcond", "pd"),   value    = c(.one(fit_det$fit$objective, digits = 10), .one(fit_det$fit$converged),                .one(fit_det$fit$counts["function"]), .one(fit_det$fit$counts["gradient"]),                .one(fit_det$fit$rcond, digits = 6), .one(fit_det$fit$pd)) )) # The probes run at n_starts = 1 ON PURPOSE. Multi-start is what makes the # reported fit robust -- it perturbs around its start until it escapes small # basins -- which is exactly what would HIDE a second basin from this check. A # single start goes where its starting point leads, so it is the thing that # actually finds another optimum if one is there. # # Only the FREE positions move. hazard() holds a fixed parameter at the value # theta gives it, so a probe that moved one would fit a different model, and # could beat the reported fit without the reported fit being in the wrong # basin. The held positions are each phase's `fixed` set, plus the shape a g3 # `constraint` derives from the others, which hazard() would replace anyway. held <- unlist(lapply(names(phases), function(nm) {   ph <- phases[[nm]]   derived <- switch(if (is.null(ph$constraint)) "none" else ph$constraint,                     alpha_gamma_eta = "alpha", eta_gamma = "eta", character(0))   p <- c(ph$fixed, derived)   paste0(nm, ".", c(p, paste0("log_", p))) })) free <- !(theta_names %in% held)  # Demo: widen or add probes if your model has more phases or free parameters. # Every row must differ from every other row: a duplicated start is a fit that # costs time and tests nothing. Move only positions where `free` is TRUE. probes <- rbind(theta0, theta0 + 0.5 * free, theta0 - 0.5 * free) if (anyDuplicated(probes)) {   stop("Two probe rows are identical: that fit costs time and tests nothing.",        call. = FALSE) } .moved <- theta_names[!free][colSums(probes[, !free, drop = FALSE] != rep(theta0[!free], each = nrow(probes))) > 0] if (length(.moved)) {   stop("A probe moves a fixed parameter (", paste(.moved, collapse = ", "), "), so it fits a different ",        "model and its log-likelihood cannot be compared with the reported fit's.", call. = FALSE) } probe_ll <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(probes)), function(i) {   f <- try(hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                   phases = phases, theta = probes[i, ], fit = TRUE,                   control = list(conserve = TRUE,                                  n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)), silent = TRUE)   if (inherits(f, "try-error")) NA_real_ else f$fit$objective }, numeric(1)) Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Hessian is not positive-definite at the optimum; standard errors may be unreliable Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Non-positive variance estimates; the optimum may not be a proper maximum Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Hessian is not positive-definite at the optimum; standard errors may be unreliable Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Non-positive variance estimates; the optimum may not be a proper maximum probe_table <- data.frame(   probe       = seq_len(nrow(probes)),   logLik      = probe_ll,   vs_reported = probe_ll - fit_det$fit$objective ) knitr::kable(probe_table, digits = 6) fit_nc <- hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                  phases = phases, theta = theta0, fit = TRUE,                  control = list(conserve = FALSE,                                 n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)) check_fit(fit_nc, "noconserve") # Sum_i Lambda(t_i) is what `conserve` pins to the event count. Reporting it # under BOTH settings is the only way a reader can tell "the control did # nothing" from "the control had almost nothing to do" -- the two are identical # in the likelihood column and mean opposite things. sum_lambda <- c(   sum(predict(fit_det, type = "cumulative_hazard")),   sum(predict(fit_nc, type = "cumulative_hazard")) ) conservation <- data.frame(   conserve   = c(TRUE, FALSE),   sum_lambda = sum_lambda,   events     = cc$n_events ) conservation$excess <- conservation$sum_lambda - conservation$events knitr::kable(conservation, digits = 6)

code: # No `condition` in control: SAS's CONDITION= option has no equivalent in # hazard(), which ignores the element with a warning in the report. The fit # reports the conditioning of its Hessian afterwards instead, as rcond below. fit_det <- hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                   phases = phases, theta = theta0, fit = TRUE,                   control = list(conserve = TRUE,                                  n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)) check_fit(fit_det, "deterministic") summary(fit_det) Multiphase hazard model (2 phases)   observations: 725    predictors:   0    dist:         multiphase    phase 1:      early - cdf (early risk)   phase 2:      late - g3 (late risk)   engine:       native-r-m2    converged:    TRUE    gradient:     relative 3.33e-06 (SAS/C requires <= 6.06e-06; met)   log-lik:      -1503.29    Not done in this run: none   evaluations: fn=6, gr=1  Coefficients (internal scale):    Phase: early (cdf)                estimate std_error     z_stat      p_value   log_mu     -3.5475335 0.6503541 -5.4547723 4.903564e-08   log_t_half -5.4139983 2.4642214 -2.1970421 2.801744e-02   nu          2.6936482 2.3449537  1.1486999 2.506797e-01   m          -0.2197872 0.4695841 -0.4680465 6.397513e-01    Phase: late (g3)             estimate  std_error    z_stat      p_value   log_mu  -2.5663963 0.17126255 -14.98516 9.180758e-51   log_tau  0.0000000         NA        NA           NA   gamma    1.0000000         NA        NA           NA   alpha    1.0000000         NA        NA           NA   eta      0.8800072 0.05681755  15.48830 4.161509e-54 # There is no logLik() method for class "hazard": the log-likelihood is # fit$fit$objective. # # rcond and pd are read OFF THE FIT rather than recomputed from vcov(): vcov() # includes every FIXED parameter as an all-NA row and column, and rcond() # cannot take an NA matrix. The fit's own values are computed on the free # parameters, which is also what SAS's condition number refers to. # # A multiphase fit reports how many times the optimizer evaluated the function # and its gradient, not an iteration count. Each value is read through .one(), # so a field a fit does not carry shows as "not reported" rather than changing # the number of rows and stopping the render. .one <- function(x, ...) if (length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x)) format(x, ...) else "not reported" knitr::kable(data.frame(   quantity = c("log-likelihood", "converged", "function evaluations", "gradient evaluations", "rcond", "pd"),   value    = c(.one(fit_det$fit$objective, digits = 10), .one(fit_det$fit$converged),                .one(fit_det$fit$counts["function"]), .one(fit_det$fit$counts["gradient"]),                .one(fit_det$fit$rcond, digits = 6), .one(fit_det$fit$pd)) ))

what: Fit 2 — did the starting point matter?
text: Table 6: Log-likelihood single-start probe fit reported fit probe beats reported fit means reported fit wrong basin, starting values need revisiting anything read.
code: # The probes run at n_starts = 1 ON PURPOSE. Multi-start is what makes the # reported fit robust -- it perturbs around its start until it escapes small # basins -- which is exactly what would HIDE a second basin from this check. A # single start goes where its starting point leads, so it is the thing that # actually finds another optimum if one is there. # # Only the FREE positions move. hazard() holds a fixed parameter at the value # theta gives it, so a probe that moved one would fit a different model, and # could beat the reported fit without the reported fit being in the wrong # basin. The held positions are each phase's `fixed` set, plus the shape a g3 # `constraint` derives from the others, which hazard() would replace anyway. held <- unlist(lapply(names(phases), function(nm) {   ph <- phases[[nm]]   derived <- switch(if (is.null(ph$constraint)) "none" else ph$constraint,                     alpha_gamma_eta = "alpha", eta_gamma = "eta", character(0))   p <- c(ph$fixed, derived)   paste0(nm, ".", c(p, paste0("log_", p))) })) free <- !(theta_names %in% held)  # Demo: widen or add probes if your model has more phases or free parameters. # Every row must differ from every other row: a duplicated start is a fit that # costs time and tests nothing. Move only positions where `free` is TRUE. probes <- rbind(theta0, theta0 + 0.5 * free, theta0 - 0.5 * free) if (anyDuplicated(probes)) {   stop("Two probe rows are identical: that fit costs time and tests nothing.",        call. = FALSE) } .moved <- theta_names[!free][colSums(probes[, !free, drop = FALSE] != rep(theta0[!free], each = nrow(probes))) > 0] if (length(.moved)) {   stop("A probe moves a fixed parameter (", paste(.moved, collapse = ", "), "), so it fits a different ",        "model and its log-likelihood cannot be compared with the reported fit's.", call. = FALSE) } probe_ll <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(probes)), function(i) {   f <- try(hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                   phases = phases, theta = probes[i, ], fit = TRUE,                   control = list(conserve = TRUE,                                  n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)), silent = TRUE)   if (inherits(f, "try-error")) NA_real_ else f$fit$objective }, numeric(1)) Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Hessian is not positive-definite at the optimum; standard errors may be unreliable Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Non-positive variance estimates; the optimum may not be a proper maximum Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Hessian is not positive-definite at the optimum; standard errors may be unreliable Warning in .hzr_safe_solve(hess_result): Non-positive variance estimates; the optimum may not be a proper maximum probe_table <- data.frame(   probe       = seq_len(nrow(probes)),   logLik      = probe_ll,   vs_reported = probe_ll - fit_det$fit$objective ) knitr::kable(probe_table, digits = 6)

code: fit_nc <- hazard(surv_formula, data = resp, dist = "multiphase",                  phases = phases, theta = theta0, fit = TRUE,                  control = list(conserve = FALSE,                                 n_starts = 1, maxit = 2000)) check_fit(fit_nc, "noconserve") # Sum_i Lambda(t_i) is what `conserve` pins to the event count. Reporting it # under BOTH settings is the only way a reader can tell "the control did # nothing" from "the control had almost nothing to do" -- the two are identical # in the likelihood column and mean opposite things. sum_lambda <- c(   sum(predict(fit_det, type = "cumulative_hazard")),   sum(predict(fit_nc, type = "cumulative_hazard")) ) conservation <- data.frame(   conserve   = c(TRUE, FALSE),   sum_lambda = sum_lambda,   events     = cc$n_events ) conservation$excess <- conservation$sum_lambda - conservation$events knitr::kable(conservation, digits = 6)

code: cf <- coef(fit_det)  # vcov() returns a scalar NA rather than a matrix when the Hessian could not be # inverted, so diag() on it errors. That is a result ABOUT the fit, not a bug # to route around: report it and carry on with what does not need curvature. V <- vcov(fit_det) se_available <- is.matrix(V) && nrow(V) == length(cf) && any(is.finite(diag(V)))  # NOTE the brace. At top level `if (a) x` <newline> `else y` is a PARSE ERROR: # `else` must not start a line outside a block. knitr captures that error into # the document and carries on, so the chunk "runs" and silently emits nothing. se <- if (se_available) {   setNames(sqrt(diag(V)), names(cf)) } else {   setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(cf)), names(cf)) }  # Demo: map your coefficients to their natural scale, and to the SAS names a # reader will be comparing against. exp() where R reports a log, identity where # it already reports the natural value. est <- data.frame(   parameter     = c("MUE", "THALF", "NU", "M", "MUL", "ETA"),   estimate      = c(exp(cf[["early.log_mu"]]), exp(cf[["early.log_t_half"]]),                     cf[["early.nu"]], cf[["early.m"]],                     exp(cf[["late.log_mu"]]), cf[["late.eta"]]),   se_on_r_scale = c(se[["early.log_mu"]], se[["early.log_t_half"]],                     se[["early.nu"]], se[["early.m"]],                     se[["late.log_mu"]], se[["late.eta"]]),   r_scale       = c("log", "log", "natural", "natural", "log", "natural"),   row.names     = NULL ) knitr::kable(est, digits = 6) # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption if (!se_available) {   no_se <- data.frame(     warning = "The Hessian could not be inverted: NO standard errors are available."   )   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-estimates-no-se",     "#| tbl-cap: \"Standard errors could not be computed\"", "knitr::kable(no_se)", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n") }

text: Figure 1: Parametric survival reported fit (solid) Kaplan-Meier estimate (dashed) 68% band (dotted).
code: # The check to make before hp or hm reads this fit: the curve should run through # the step function for the whole of follow-up. A curve that leaves the band # early or late names the phase that is misspecified, which the log-likelihood # and the estimates above cannot. hp draws the same overlay against the ac life # table for publication; this one is drawn from the rows fitted here. # An interval-censored response has no Kaplan-Meier estimate, so its figure # shows the parametric curve alone. # The last finite time, as an interval-censored response may code an open upper bound as Inf. .times <- unlist(resp[intersect(c("time", "lo", "hi"), names(resp))], use.names = FALSE) .grid <- data.frame(time = seq(0, max(.times[is.finite(.times)]), length.out = 200)) .grid$survival <- 100 * unname(predict(fit_det, newdata = .grid, type = "survival")) .fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(.grid, ggplot2::aes(x = .data$time, y = .data$survival)) if (!all(c("lo", "hi") %in% names(resp))) {   # 68%, one standard error either side, as hp and the SAS plots draw it.   .km <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = resp, conf.int = 0.68268948)   .km <- data.frame(time = c(0, .km$time), survival = 100 * c(1, .km$surv),                     lower = 100 * c(1, .km$lower), upper = 100 * c(1, .km$upper))   .fig <- .fig +     ggplot2::geom_step(data = .km, ggplot2::aes(y = .data$lower), linetype = "dotted", na.rm = TRUE) +     ggplot2::geom_step(data = .km, ggplot2::aes(y = .data$upper), linetype = "dotted", na.rm = TRUE) +     ggplot2::geom_step(data = .km, linetype = "dashed") } .fig <- .fig +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +   ggplot2::labs(x = "Years", y = "Survival (%)") +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(.fig, "hz-fit") .fig

# `hp` plots what this writes and `hm` fixes its shape parameters at these # values, both by set. A job that persists nothing cannot be chained from. hz_art <- list(deterministic = fit_det, noconserve = fit_nc,                phases = phases, theta0 = theta0) hz_art <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(   hz_art,   data = .provenance_data,   analysis = list(     time = list(variable = TIME),     event = list(variable = EVENT, event = 1L, censored = 0L)   ),   cohort = cc,   # hm, hp and hs rebuild exactly these rows from this record, and take TIME   # and EVENT from it, so the chain cannot drift from the fit it builds on.   selection = c(attr(job_data$record, "selection"), list(time = TIME, event = EVENT)) ) saveRDS(hz_art, set_path("estimates", "hz.rds"))

code: # Demo: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset). DATASET <- "built"  # Demo: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset. ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL  # Demo: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row: #   WHERE <- quote(age >= 18) #   WHERE <- rlang::exprs(age >= 18, hx_chf == 1) WHERE <- NULL  # Demo: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN; # name another column, such as "randid", if the study uses one. ID <- "patient_id"  # Demo: what makes a row unique; one row per patient unless repeated measures # add their visit time or date, for example KEY <- c(ID, "iv_echo"). KEY <- ID  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one # registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key; #     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last", #     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column #     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE" #     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record #     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq") #     breaks it. This job models one row per #     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  # Demo: the event, a 0/1 column, 1 for a patient who had it (the SAS macro's # EVENT=). TRUE and FALSE also work. A patient with no value is ranked with the # rest, as in SAS, but counts toward no group's rate: not in its patients, its # events or, under "hazard", its follow-up. EVENT <- "dead"  # Demo: the link, the scale the group rates are put on before they are plotted. # "hazard" is the log of the constant hazard rate, log(events / sum of follow-up), # for an event with variable follow-up such as death (the SAS call's cox=1). # "logit" is log(p / (1 - p)), for an event every patient was followed to the same # point for, such as in-hospital death or a complication. LINK <- "hazard"  # Demo: the follow-up column, in the unit the study reports (years here). Only # "hazard" reads it, and INTERVAL below reads it for either link. A patient with # no value is left out of a "hazard" calibration, as the SAS macro left them out. TIME <- "iv_dead"  # Demo: NULL, or a window on follow-up, c(start, end), such as c(0.25, 5): one phase # of a hazard, the SAS early, constant or late phase, in the unit of TIME. A patient # whose follow-up ended before `start` is left out and counted. Everyone else is # censored at `end`: a patient followed past it counts as followed to `end`, and an # event after it does not count. Under "hazard" the time at risk is then the time # inside the window, TIME capped at `end`, less `start`; the SAS template summed it # from 0. Under "logit" the same patients are kept and an event counts only if it # falls inside the window. Both counts are reported under the data table. INTERVAL <- NULL  # Demo: the covariates to calibrate, one row each. `name` is a column of the data; # `kind` is "continuous" (ranked into groups) or "ordinal" (each level is a # group). The other columns are optional, and a covariate that does not give # one takes the default: #   groups    5      how many groups a continuous covariate is ranked into; the #                    job stops if any group has fewer than 5 patients, and for #                    an ordinal covariate (at most 20 levels) if any level has #   constant  the covariate's median to one significant figure; the c in the #             inverse, inverse squared, squared and exponential scales. A #             median that rounds to 0 (a 0/1 indicator) leaves it NA, and #             those four scales are not computable until you set one #   shift     0      added before the log, for a covariate that can be 0 #   label     the name   the heading over its table and figure #   chosen    NA     the scale to use: "raw", "log", "inverse", #                    "inverse_squared", "squared" or "exp". Leave it NA until #                    you have seen the figure; the job then warns, and a final #                    render stops until every covariate has one. VARIABLES <- data.frame(   name   = c("age", "nyha_pr"),   kind   = c("continuous", "ordinal"),   chosen = c("raw", "raw") )  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("lg-age"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

code: # Demo: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset). DATASET <- "built"  # Demo: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset. ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL  # Demo: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row: #   WHERE <- quote(age >= 18) #   WHERE <- rlang::exprs(age >= 18, hx_chf == 1) WHERE <- quote(as.integer(format(dt_surg, "%Y")) < 2015)  # Demo: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN; # name another column, such as "randid", if the study uses one. ID <- "patient_id"  # Demo: what makes a row unique; one row per patient unless repeated measures # add their visit time or date, for example KEY <- c(ID, "iv_echo"). KEY <- ID  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one # registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key; #     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last", #     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column #     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE" #     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record #     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq") #     breaks it. This job models one row per #     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  OUTCOME <- "stroke" PREDICTORS <- c("age", "female", "hx_chf", "hx_dm", "lvef", "bmi") OUTCOME_LEVELS <- c("no", "yes") EVENT_LEVEL <- "yes" IMPUTATION <- NULL # Stacked imputations repeat each patient once per imputation. if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) KEY <- unique(c(KEY, IMPUTATION)) # The checksum of every dataset in manifest.yaml is checked before anything is # read, so a result can name the data that produced it. It stops on a mismatch. hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,                                           where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,                                           reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY, one_row_per_patient = TRUE,                                           imputation = IMPUTATION) # This job's data are the model's training data, which lm-checkpred tells from its validation data. job_data$provenance$role <- "training" if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) job_data$provenance_join$role <- "training" d <- job_data$data .provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) # The identifier column read_job_data() used: MRN or eMRN when there is no ccfid. .id <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$id # The imputation column read_job_data() matched, in the data's own spelling. IMPUTATION <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$imputation knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) # A column the study choices name that the data lack stops here, naming the setting to change. hvtiRtemplates:::.check_job_columns(d, OUTCOME = OUTCOME, PREDICTORS = PREDICTORS) # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption if (!is.null(job_data$attrition)) {   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-data-attrition",     paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(paste0("Analysis set `", ANALYSIS_SET, "`: exclusions, in order"), quote = "\"")),     "knitr::kable(job_data$attrition)", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n") } # The fit drops a row missing any model variable, so the cohort it uses is said here, # counted within one imputation when the data are multiply imputed. .missing_values <- hvtiRtemplates:::.missing_cases(d, OUTCOME = OUTCOME, PREDICTORS = PREDICTORS,                                                    imputation = IMPUTATION) knitr::kable(.missing_values) model_formula <- stats::reformulate(PREDICTORS, response = OUTCOME) fit <- hvtiRpropensity::fit_logistic(   model_formula, d, family = "binary", outcome_col = OUTCOME, id_col = .id,   imputation_col = IMPUTATION, outcome_levels = OUTCOME_LEVELS,   event_level = EVENT_LEVEL, prediction_prefix = "predicted" )

A later job reattaches its own data by digesting its IDs with the same key: see lm-checkpred. saveRDS(hvtiRtemplates:::.digest_bundle_ids(fit, .root), MODEL_PATH)

# Demo: the bar width on the 0 to 100 score scale. 5 suits most cohorts; use 10 # for a small one, and 1 for a rare treatment whose scores sit near zero. BINWIDTH <- 5  # Optional, and needs no edit: the saved bundle. NULL in MODEL_SET is this # job's own set, where the bundle is when SUBJECT and TYPE match the # lm-propensity_binary job's. A mirror job in a set of its own names that job's # set, "<subject>-<type>", for example MODEL_SET <- "treatment-propensity". MODEL_FILE <- "lm-propensity_binary.rds" MODEL_SET <- "approach-propensity"  # Optional, and needs no edit: the group labels. NULL labels each group by its # treatment level, as the propensity job declared it. To relabel, name both # levels by the treatment column's own values, as they appear in the data; for # a 0/1 column that is GROUP_LABELS <- c("0" = "Surgical", "1" = "Transcatheter"). GROUP_LABELS <- c(surgical = "Surgical", transcatheter = "Transcatheter")  # Optional, and needs no edit: a pair-match flag, 1 for a matched patient. NULL # draws no matched figure. A study whose dataset carries a flag, from a SAS # match for example, names that column, and DATASET and ID say where to read # it. The flag is joined onto the bundle's patients by a study-keyed digest of # ID, so no identifier is kept or printed. MATCH <- "match_pair" DATASET <- "built" ID <- "patient_id"  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("lp-mirror-weighted"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL # unnumbered: defines the figure helpers and shows nothing # The figure helpers. Each takes what it draws as an argument, so the tests # call them on synthetic data.  # The two groups, treated first. hv_mirror_hist()'s help says control first and # treated above, but the hvtiPlotR 2.8.5 code draws the FIRST level above, so # treated is passed first and mirror_hist() checks the sign at run time. # Labeled by the levels the propensity job declared, or by # GROUP_LABELS, named by those levels. mirror_groups <- function(meta, labels = NULL) {   declared <- as.character(meta$treatment_levels)   treated <- as.character(meta$treated_level)   if (length(declared) != 2L || anyNA(declared) || length(treated) != 1L || !treated %in% declared) {     stop("The saved bundle does not declare two treatment levels and the treated one: rebuild it by ",          "rendering the lm-propensity_binary job with the current template.", call. = FALSE)   }   levels <- c(treated, setdiff(declared, treated))   if (is.null(labels)) return(list(levels = levels, labels = levels))   if (!is.character(labels) || length(labels) != 2L || anyNA(labels) || is.null(names(labels)) ||         !setequal(names(labels), declared)) {     stop("GROUP_LABELS must be NULL or two labels named by the treatment levels, such as c(",          paste0(declared, " = \"", declared, "\"", collapse = ", "), ").", call. = FALSE)   }   list(levels = levels, labels = unname(labels[levels])) }  # The y-axis limit: the tallest bar on either side, plus a tenth of it and at # least 1, as hv_mirror_hist() pads. The same limit above and below, so both # groups are read on one scale. mirror_limit <- function(y) {   top <- max(abs(y), 0)   top + max(1, ceiling(0.1 * top)) }  # One hv_mirror_hist() object. `scores` has one row per patient: score, group, # weight and matched. The unmatched figure keeps only the all-patient bars. mirror_hist <- function(scores, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched"), groups, binwidth) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   args <- list(scores, score_col = "score", group_col = "group", group_levels = groups$levels,                group_labels = groups$labels, binwidth = binwidth)   if (identical(kind, "weighted")) {     args$weight_col <- "weight"   } else {     args$match_col <- "matched"     args$matched_value <- 1L   }   mh <- suppressMessages(do.call(hvtiPlotR::hv_mirror_hist, args))   if (identical(kind, "unmatched")) mh$data <- mh$data[mh$data$layer == "Before", , drop = FALSE]   # Treated must be above the axis. A different hvtiPlotR may draw the first   # level below it, and a figure with the groups swapped reads as the opposite.   if (any(mh$data$y[mh$data$group == groups$labels[1L]] < 0, na.rm = TRUE) ||         any(mh$data$y[mh$data$group == groups$labels[2L]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {     stop("hv_mirror_hist() in the installed hvtiPlotR (", utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR"), ") draws the ",          "treated group below the axis: its orientation changed since 2.8.5, which this job was written ",          "against. Update the job for that hvtiPlotR before drawing the figure.", call. = FALSE)   }   mh }  # The figure: the derived symmetric axis, and a fill that names each layer. mirror_figure <- function(mh, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched")) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   limit <- mirror_limit(mh$data$y)   breaks <- pretty(c(-limit, limit), n = 8)   mh$meta$lower <- -limit   mh$meta$upper <- limit   mh$meta$y_breaks <- breaks[abs(breaks) <= limit]   labels <- mh$meta$group_labels   colors <- hvtiPlotR::hv_palette(2L)   fill <- switch(kind,     unmatched = c(before_g0 = colors[[1L]], before_g1 = colors[[2L]]),     weighted = c(before_g0 = "gray85", before_g1 = "gray85", weighted_g0 = colors[[1L]], weighted_g1 = colors[[2L]]),     matched = c(before_g0 = "gray85", before_g1 = "gray85", matched_g0 = colors[[1L]], matched_g1 = colors[[2L]])   )   # The gray all-patient bars are one legend entry, not one a group.   shown <- if (identical(kind, "unmatched")) names(fill) else names(fill)[-2L]   names_shown <- switch(kind,     unmatched = labels,     weighted = c("All patients", paste(labels, "(weighted)")),     matched = c("All patients", paste(labels, "(matched)"))   )   plot(mh) +     ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fill, breaks = shown, labels = names_shown, name = NULL) +     ggplot2::labs(x = "Propensity score (%)",                   y = if (identical(kind, "weighted")) "Patients, or sum of matching weights" else "Patients") +     hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) +     ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top") }  # Patients in each group; the sum of the matching weights for the weighted # figure, and the matched patients for the matched one. Counts only. mirror_counts <- function(mh, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched")) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   w <- mh$tables$working   levels <- mh$meta$group_levels   out <- data.frame(group = mh$meta$group_labels,                     patients = vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$group == g), integer(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE))   if (identical(kind, "weighted")) {     out$weighted <- vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$weight[w$group == g]), numeric(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE)   }   if (identical(kind, "matched")) {     out$matched <- vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$group == g & w$matched == 1L), integer(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE)   }   out }  # The match flag of each bundle patient, joined by ID digest. `ids` are the # dataset's identifiers made comparable with the bundle's by .bundle_ids(), # and `flag` the MATCH column. Returns the 0/1 flag for each bundle patient # and the two counts the job reports; stops when fewer than half of the # bundle's patients are in the dataset, when the flag is not coded 0 and 1, or # when no scored patient has a 1. mirror_join <- function(bundle_ids, ids, flag) {   if (anyDuplicated(ids[!is.na(ids)])) {     stop("The dataset holds a patient more than once, so the match flag cannot be joined one to one: set ",          "DATASET to a dataset with one row per patient.", call. = FALSE)   }   at <- match(bundle_ids, ids, incomparables = NA)   joined <- !is.na(at)   if (sum(joined) < length(bundle_ids) / 2) {     stop("Only ", sum(joined), " of the ", length(bundle_ids), " patients the scores were computed for are in ",          "the dataset read for MATCH. The dataset is not the cohort the scores came from, or its ID does not ",          "identify patients as the propensity job's did: check DATASET and ID.", call. = FALSE)   }   value <- flag[at]   if (is.logical(value)) value <- as.integer(value)   seen <- unique(value[!is.na(value)])   if (!all(seen %in% c(0, 1))) {     stop("MATCH must be coded 0 and 1 (or TRUE and FALSE), 1 for a matched patient: the column holds ",          length(seen), " distinct values for the scored patients, not all 0 or 1. Recode it, or change MATCH ",          "in edit-study-choices.", call. = FALSE)   }   if (!any(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE)) {     stop("MATCH flags no scored patient as matched (none has a 1): check that MATCH names the pair-match ",          "flag, with 1 for a matched patient, and that DATASET and ID read the right file.", call. = FALSE)   }   # A dataset row with no flag is not a flagged patient, so it is left out of the second count.   list(     matched = as.integer(!is.na(value) & value == 1),     counts = data.frame(       count = c("Patients with a score and no match flag", "Patients with a match flag and no score"),       patients = c(sum(is.na(value)), sum(!is.na(ids) & !is.na(flag) & !ids %in% bundle_ids))     )   ) }

code: # MODEL_FILE is a file name and MODEL_SET a set name, so neither can reach # outside the study's estimates. MODEL_PATH <- hvtiRtemplates:::.handoff_path(MODEL_FILE, MODEL_SET, .root, function(file) set_path("estimates", file),                                              upstream = "lm-propensity_binary", set_example = "treatment-propensity") .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) # A bundle without its lineage stops here with the job to render again. .model_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(MODEL_PATH, "propensity-model", .cfg, "the lm-propensity_binary job") bundle <- .model_read$value .meta <- bundle$meta .cols <- c(.meta$id_col, .meta$treatment_col, .meta$score_col, .meta$weight_col) if (!inherits(bundle, "ps_logistic") || length(.cols) != 4L || !all(.cols %in% names(bundle$data))) {   stop("The saved bundle is not a binary propensity model with its patients, treatment, score and matching ",        "weight: rebuild it by rendering the lm-propensity_binary job with the current template.", call. = FALSE) } .provenance_data <- .model_read$lineage$data .provenance_artifacts <- c(.model_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.model_read$record)) # The data are read again as the propensity job read them. The rebuilt read must # have the same rows, the same patients and the same hash of the study-keyed IDs # (the same patients) as the bundle's lineage, and the manifest must verify. hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .up <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(   .cfg, .model_read$lineage, list(), source = MODEL_FILE,   rerun = "Render the lm-propensity_binary job again with the current template, then this one." ) job_data <- .up$job_data .provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) # One row per patient: the score, the treatment, the matching weight and the # patient's ID digest, which only the MATCH join reads. groups <- mirror_groups(.meta, GROUP_LABELS) scores <- data.frame(   id = bundle$data[[.meta$id_col]],   score = bundle$data[[.meta$score_col]],   group = as.character(bundle$data[[.meta$treatment_col]]),   weight = bundle$data[[.meta$weight_col]],   matched = 0L ) .bad <- c(`with a missing score` = sum(is.na(scores$score)),           `with a missing matching weight` = sum(is.na(scores$weight)),           `with a missing treatment` = sum(is.na(scores$group)),           `in a group the bundle does not declare` = sum(!is.na(scores$group) & !scores$group %in% groups$levels)) if (any(.bad > 0)) {   .bad <- .bad[.bad > 0]   stop("The saved bundle holds ", paste0(.bad, " patient", ifelse(.bad == 1, "", "s"), " ", names(.bad), collapse = ", "),        "; a mirrored histogram draws only patients with a score, a weight and a declared group. Rebuild it by ",        "rendering the lm-propensity_binary job with the current template.", call. = FALSE) } if (anyDuplicated(scores$id)) {   stop("The saved bundle holds a patient more than once; a mirrored histogram counts each patient once. ",        "Rebuild it by rendering the lm-propensity_binary job with the current template.", call. = FALSE) } # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption # The flag is joined by a digest of ID under the study key, the digest the # bundle holds, so this job keeps and prints no identifier. A scored patient # with no flag is drawn as unmatched and counted, never dropped. .join <- NULL if (!is.null(MATCH)) {   if (!is.character(MATCH) || length(MATCH) != 1L || is.na(MATCH)) {     stop("MATCH must be NULL or one column name.", call. = FALSE)   }   match_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, id = ID, one_row_per_patient = TRUE)   match_data$provenance$role <- "match"   .provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, list(match_data$provenance))   .id <- attr(match_data$record, "selection")$id   # .check_job_columns() reads a setting as formula terms, so "age + sex" and "."   # would pass it; MATCH is one column.   if (!MATCH %in% names(match_data$data)) {     stop("MATCH names a column this dataset does not have: ", MATCH, ". Change MATCH in edit-study-choices.",          call. = FALSE)   }   hvtiRtemplates:::.check_job_columns(match_data$data, MATCH = MATCH)   if (!identical(tolower(.id), tolower(.meta$id_col))) {     stop("The dataset read for MATCH identifies patients by `", .id, "`, the bundle by `", .meta$id_col,          "`: set ID so both use the same identifier.", call. = FALSE)   }   .join <- mirror_join(scores$id, hvtiRtemplates:::.bundle_ids(bundle, match_data$data[[.id]], .root),                        match_data$data[[MATCH]])   scores$matched <- .join$matched   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-match-join",     "#| tbl-cap: \"The match flag joined onto the scored patients\"",     "knitr::kable(.join$counts, col.names = c(\"\", \"Patients\"))", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n") } knitr::kable(.join$counts, col.names = c("", "Patients"))

The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL # unnumbered: defines the figure helpers and shows nothing # The figure helpers. Each takes what it draws as an argument, so the tests # call them on synthetic data.  # The two groups, treated first. hv_mirror_hist()'s help says control first and # treated above, but the hvtiPlotR 2.8.5 code draws the FIRST level above, so # treated is passed first and mirror_hist() checks the sign at run time. # Labeled by the levels the propensity job declared, or by # GROUP_LABELS, named by those levels. mirror_groups <- function(meta, labels = NULL) {   declared <- as.character(meta$treatment_levels)   treated <- as.character(meta$treated_level)   if (length(declared) != 2L || anyNA(declared) || length(treated) != 1L || !treated %in% declared) {     stop("The saved bundle does not declare two treatment levels and the treated one: rebuild it by ",          "rendering the lm-propensity_binary job with the current template.", call. = FALSE)   }   levels <- c(treated, setdiff(declared, treated))   if (is.null(labels)) return(list(levels = levels, labels = levels))   if (!is.character(labels) || length(labels) != 2L || anyNA(labels) || is.null(names(labels)) ||         !setequal(names(labels), declared)) {     stop("GROUP_LABELS must be NULL or two labels named by the treatment levels, such as c(",          paste0(declared, " = \"", declared, "\"", collapse = ", "), ").", call. = FALSE)   }   list(levels = levels, labels = unname(labels[levels])) }  # The y-axis limit: the tallest bar on either side, plus a tenth of it and at # least 1, as hv_mirror_hist() pads. The same limit above and below, so both # groups are read on one scale. mirror_limit <- function(y) {   top <- max(abs(y), 0)   top + max(1, ceiling(0.1 * top)) }  # One hv_mirror_hist() object. `scores` has one row per patient: score, group, # weight and matched. The unmatched figure keeps only the all-patient bars. mirror_hist <- function(scores, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched"), groups, binwidth) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   args <- list(scores, score_col = "score", group_col = "group", group_levels = groups$levels,                group_labels = groups$labels, binwidth = binwidth)   if (identical(kind, "weighted")) {     args$weight_col <- "weight"   } else {     args$match_col <- "matched"     args$matched_value <- 1L   }   mh <- suppressMessages(do.call(hvtiPlotR::hv_mirror_hist, args))   if (identical(kind, "unmatched")) mh$data <- mh$data[mh$data$layer == "Before", , drop = FALSE]   # Treated must be above the axis. A different hvtiPlotR may draw the first   # level below it, and a figure with the groups swapped reads as the opposite.   if (any(mh$data$y[mh$data$group == groups$labels[1L]] < 0, na.rm = TRUE) ||         any(mh$data$y[mh$data$group == groups$labels[2L]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {     stop("hv_mirror_hist() in the installed hvtiPlotR (", utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR"), ") draws the ",          "treated group below the axis: its orientation changed since 2.8.5, which this job was written ",          "against. Update the job for that hvtiPlotR before drawing the figure.", call. = FALSE)   }   mh }  # The figure: the derived symmetric axis, and a fill that names each layer. mirror_figure <- function(mh, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched")) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   limit <- mirror_limit(mh$data$y)   breaks <- pretty(c(-limit, limit), n = 8)   mh$meta$lower <- -limit   mh$meta$upper <- limit   mh$meta$y_breaks <- breaks[abs(breaks) <= limit]   labels <- mh$meta$group_labels   colors <- hvtiPlotR::hv_palette(2L)   fill <- switch(kind,     unmatched = c(before_g0 = colors[[1L]], before_g1 = colors[[2L]]),     weighted = c(before_g0 = "gray85", before_g1 = "gray85", weighted_g0 = colors[[1L]], weighted_g1 = colors[[2L]]),     matched = c(before_g0 = "gray85", before_g1 = "gray85", matched_g0 = colors[[1L]], matched_g1 = colors[[2L]])   )   # The gray all-patient bars are one legend entry, not one a group.   shown <- if (identical(kind, "unmatched")) names(fill) else names(fill)[-2L]   names_shown <- switch(kind,     unmatched = labels,     weighted = c("All patients", paste(labels, "(weighted)")),     matched = c("All patients", paste(labels, "(matched)"))   )   plot(mh) +     ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fill, breaks = shown, labels = names_shown, name = NULL) +     ggplot2::labs(x = "Propensity score (%)",                   y = if (identical(kind, "weighted")) "Patients, or sum of matching weights" else "Patients") +     hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) +     ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top") }  # Patients in each group; the sum of the matching weights for the weighted # figure, and the matched patients for the matched one. Counts only. mirror_counts <- function(mh, kind = c("unmatched", "weighted", "matched")) {   kind <- match.arg(kind)   w <- mh$tables$working   levels <- mh$meta$group_levels   out <- data.frame(group = mh$meta$group_labels,                     patients = vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$group == g), integer(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE))   if (identical(kind, "weighted")) {     out$weighted <- vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$weight[w$group == g]), numeric(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE)   }   if (identical(kind, "matched")) {     out$matched <- vapply(levels, function(g) sum(w$group == g & w$matched == 1L), integer(1L), USE.NAMES = FALSE)   }   out }  # The match flag of each bundle patient, joined by ID digest. `ids` are the # dataset's identifiers made comparable with the bundle's by .bundle_ids(), # and `flag` the MATCH column. Returns the 0/1 flag for each bundle patient # and the two counts the job reports; stops when fewer than half of the # bundle's patients are in the dataset, when the flag is not coded 0 and 1, or # when no scored patient has a 1. mirror_join <- function(bundle_ids, ids, flag) {   if (anyDuplicated(ids[!is.na(ids)])) {     stop("The dataset holds a patient more than once, so the match flag cannot be joined one to one: set ",          "DATASET to a dataset with one row per patient.", call. = FALSE)   }   at <- match(bundle_ids, ids, incomparables = NA)   joined <- !is.na(at)   if (sum(joined) < length(bundle_ids) / 2) {     stop("Only ", sum(joined), " of the ", length(bundle_ids), " patients the scores were computed for are in ",          "the dataset read for MATCH. The dataset is not the cohort the scores came from, or its ID does not ",          "identify patients as the propensity job's did: check DATASET and ID.", call. = FALSE)   }   value <- flag[at]   if (is.logical(value)) value <- as.integer(value)   seen <- unique(value[!is.na(value)])   if (!all(seen %in% c(0, 1))) {     stop("MATCH must be coded 0 and 1 (or TRUE and FALSE), 1 for a matched patient: the column holds ",          length(seen), " distinct values for the scored patients, not all 0 or 1. Recode it, or change MATCH ",          "in edit-study-choices.", call. = FALSE)   }   if (!any(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE)) {     stop("MATCH flags no scored patient as matched (none has a 1): check that MATCH names the pair-match ",          "flag, with 1 for a matched patient, and that DATASET and ID read the right file.", call. = FALSE)   }   # A dataset row with no flag is not a flagged patient, so it is left out of the second count.   list(     matched = as.integer(!is.na(value) & value == 1),     counts = data.frame(       count = c("Patients with a score and no match flag", "Patients with a match flag and no score"),       patients = c(sum(is.na(value)), sum(!is.na(ids) & !is.na(flag) & !ids %in% bundle_ids))     )   ) }

code: # Demo: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset). DATASET <- "echo"  # Demo: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset. ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL  # Demo: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row: #   WHERE <- quote(age >= 18) #   WHERE <- rlang::exprs(age >= 18, hx_chf == 1) WHERE <- NULL  # Demo: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN; # name another column, such as "randid", if the study uses one. ID <- "patient_id"  # Demo: the visit time, in years. The data hold one row per visit, built # upstream, so the time is part of what makes a row unique. With JOIN below, # the visit time may be a column of the joined dataset alone: KEY is then # checked on the joined rows. TIME <- "iv_echo"  # Demo: what makes a row unique. The ID alone does not: a patient has a row per # visit. A duplicated visit then stops the read rather than double-counting. KEY <- c(ID, TIME)  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one # registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key; #     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last", #     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column #     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE" #     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record #     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq") #     breaks it. A job that counts or models #     patients, one row each, needs REDUCE: NULL would count every record. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  # Demo: the response measured at each visit, and its kind: "continuous", # "binary", "ordinal" or "nominal". RESPONSE <- "lvef" FAMILY   <- "continuous"  # Demo: the predictors, or NULL for every other column, which is what the # studies this template came from all did. NULL leaves out the ID, every KEY # column, the time, the response, and any ccfid, MRN or eMRN column; it takes # everything else, dates included. Name the predictors when the built dataset # carries dates or derived outcomes that should not drive the fit. PREDICTORS <- NULL  # Demo: boosting iterations and the learning rate. Studies used 0.01 to 0.05; a # smaller NU needs a larger M. The error path below says whether M was enough: # the cross-validated best M should sit well inside it, not at its right edge. M  <- 200 NU <- 0.05  # Demo: predictors tried at each split of each tree, or NULL for every one of # them, boostmtree's default. Fewer than all makes the trees less alike, as in a # random forest, at the cost of a noisier single tree; set it to reproduce a # study that fitted with a smaller mtry. A different MTRY is a different fit, so # it is part of the cache key. MTRY <- NULL  # Demo: cores for the cross-validated fit, whose cost grows with the square of # the number of patients; about 80% of it runs in parallel, so speed levels off # near 4 to 5 times however many cores you give it. Each core is a forked copy of # R holding its own working data, and memory, not speed, is what limits CORES on # a large study. The fit refuses to start, in the first minutes, when this session's # memory cannot hold it at this CORES, and says which Workbench profile to start; # the measurements behind that estimate are in R/fit-memory.R and ?guard_memory. # Run time at M = 1000, by patients and cores (2026-10-19, boostmtree 2.0.4, ordinal): # about 7 h at 1,000 patients on 4 cores, 5 h at 1,000 on 8, 22 h at 2,000 on 8 and # 110 h at 4,000 on 4. On 2.0.8 (2026-10-21, continuous, 1,391 patients, M = 1000, # 8 cores) the fit took about 1 h. Hours scale with M. # CORES should never exceed the session's CPUs; Windows cannot fork. # Not part of the cache key: the fit is identical on any number of cores. CORES <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else 4L  # Demo: seeds the fit and the sample of patients the trajectory plot draws, so # the report reproduces. Part of the cache key. SEED <- 2026  # Demo: the variables to draw partial effects for, or NULL for the six most # important. N_TRACES patients are sampled for the trajectory plot; Inf draws # every one. EFFECT_VARIABLES <- NULL N_TRACES <- 100  # Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the # render instead of returning the old fit; TRUE recomputes it. REFIT <- FALSE  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,                                           where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,                                           reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY) d <- job_data$data .provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) .selection <- attr(job_data$record, "selection") .id <- .selection$id # The data's own spelling of TIME and RESPONSE, matched ignoring case as the # ID and KEY are, so "IV_ECHO" finds iv_echo. Later chunks use these names. .resolve <- function(x) {   hit <- match(tolower(x), tolower(names(d)))   ifelse(is.na(hit), x, names(d)[hit]) } .time <- .resolve(TIME) .response <- .resolve(RESPONSE) # The fit groups visits by patient, so the ID, the rest of KEY and the visit # time are its structure, not its predictors; a predictor named for any of them # would let the model learn who a patient is or when they were seen. A known # identifier column is never a predictor either, whatever ID names: boostmtree # keeps its predictors, so one would reach the cache and the saved fit. .not_predictors <- unique(c(.id, .selection$key, .time, "ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names)) if (is.null(PREDICTORS)) {   .identifiers <- names(d)[tolower(names(d)) %in% c("ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names) & names(d) != .id]   .predictors <- names(d)[!tolower(names(d)) %in% tolower(c(.not_predictors, .response))]   if (length(.identifiers)) {     cat("Identifier columns left out of the predictors: ", paste(.identifiers, collapse = ", "), "
", sep = "")   } } else {   .predictors <- PREDICTORS } .duplicated <- unique(.predictors[duplicated(.predictors)]) if (length(.duplicated)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a variable more than once: ", paste(.duplicated, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } .structural <- .predictors[tolower(.predictors) %in% tolower(.not_predictors)] if (length(.structural)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names an identifier, a KEY column or the visit time: ", paste(.structural, collapse = ", "),        ".", call. = FALSE) } # The response predicting itself would fit perfectly and mean nothing. if (tolower(.response) %in% tolower(.predictors)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names the response (", .response, ").", call. = FALSE) } # Nor may an identifier be the response or the visit time: boostmtree keeps # both, so one would reach the cache and the saved fit. That covers the ID this # job uses and any other identifier column the data carry, such as a ccfid # beside an ID of randid. .identifier_cols <- c(.id, "ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names) if (tolower(.response) %in% tolower(.identifier_cols)) {   stop("A patient identifier (", .response, ") cannot be the response.", call. = FALSE) } if (tolower(.time) %in% tolower(.identifier_cols)) {   stop("A patient identifier (", .time, ") cannot be the visit time.", call. = FALSE) } .missing <- setdiff(c(.time, .response, .predictors), names(d)) if (length(.missing)) {   stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE) } d <- d[, c(.id, .time, .response, .predictors), drop = FALSE] # boostmtree imputes a missing predictor but cannot learn from a visit with no # response, so those visits are dropped here, and counted. .no_response <- is.na(d[[.response]]) if (any(.no_response)) {   cat(sum(.no_response), " visit(s) have no ", .response, " and are left out.
", sep = "")   d <- d[!.no_response, , drop = FALSE] } .chr <- .predictors[vapply(d[.predictors], is.character, logical(1L))] if (length(.chr)) {   d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor)   cat("Text predictors converted to factors: ", paste(.chr, collapse = ", "), "
", sep = "") } # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption if (!is.null(job_data$attrition)) {   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-data-attrition",     paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(paste0("Analysis set `", ANALYSIS_SET, "`: exclusions, in order"), quote = """)),     "knitr::kable(job_data$attrition)", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "
") }

code: # The fit groups visits by patient through `id`. It is given the study-keyed # digest of each patient's ID, not the ID: a boostmtree fit stores the ID in # several places, its base learners included, and every one of them is saved # with it. A digest still groups the visits; it cannot be read back. CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "nb-boostmtree.rds")) # The fit runs for hours at study size. Started from the console it dies with # the session, so an uncached fit is refused there: run the job with # hvtiRtemplates::submit_job() instead. Once cached, these chunks load it. hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("nb-boostmtree-fit", dir = CACHE_DIR,                                why = "a cross-validated boostmtree fit takes hours at study size",                                refit = REFIT) .patient <- hvtiRtemplates:::.id_digest(d[[.id]], hvtiRtemplates:::.study_id_key(.root)) # The fit, quoted once so the memory check below and cache_fit() read the same call: a # cache_fit() of a quoted call keys the call, so a fit cached before this was quoted still loads. .fit_code <- quote(   boostmtree(x = d[.predictors], tm = d[[.time]], id = .patient, y = d[[.response]],              family = FAMILY, M = M, nu = NU, mtry = MTRY, mod.grad = TRUE, cv.flag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE,              # get() keeps CORES out of cache_fit()'s key, which sees only the values              # the call names directly: changing it must not mark an identical fit stale.              control = boostmtree.control(cv.cores = get("CORES")),              # Reports each boosting iteration to <job>.run.progress and the render log.              # get() keeps the job's run record out of the cache key's inputs, as for              # CORES: it changes what is reported, never what is fitted.              # The fit keeps the reporter (boostmtree's formula environment holds it), which              # is safe because the reporter's frame holds only `unit`: no run record is              # saved with the fit.              progress = get(".job")$progress("iteration")) ) # Refuses here, in the first minutes of the render, a fit this session's memory cannot hold, and # names the Workbench profile to start; the numbers behind the estimate are in hvtiRtemplates' # R/fit-memory.R. A cached fit is only loaded, so it needs nothing. Whether cache_fit() will fit # is its own decision, asked the way it makes it: a file whose key matches loads even with REFIT # left TRUE, and a stale file stops it before any fit unless REFIT is set. The call itself is # unconditional, so a cached rerender still records the memory check that run_job() waits for. .need <- function(k) hvtiRtemplates:::.boostmtree_need_gib(length(unique(.patient)), nrow(d), FAMILY, k, M) .fitting <- hvtiRutilities::cache_would_fit("nb-boostmtree-fit", .fit_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) hvtiRtemplates::guard_memory(if (.fitting) .need(CORES) else 0,                              sprintf("this boostmtree fit (%s patients, %s visits, %s)",                                      format(length(unique(.patient)), big.mark = ","), format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","),                                      FAMILY),                              cores = CORES, cores_fit = .need) fit <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree-fit", .fit_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)

knitr::kable(data.frame(   quantity = c("Family", "Iterations (M)", "Learning rate (nu)", "Patients", "Visits"),   value = c(FAMILY, M, NU, length(unique(.patient)), nrow(d)) ), col.names = c("", "")) # A continuous or binary fit has one response component; an ordinal or nominal # fit has one per level after the first, each with its own cross-validated best # M and error path (fit$err.rate is then a list). Read the error at the best M # from the standardized l2 column, the scale gg_boost_error() plots. .err <- if (is.matrix(fit$err.rate)) list(fit$err.rate) else fit$err.rate # Each component is named by the level that defines it, which boostmtree keeps # in fit$q.set: a threshold for an ordinal fit, a class compared against the # reference class for a binary or nominal one. partial.plot() selects a # component by the same label ("response" for a continuous fit). .labels <- if (identical(fit$family, "continuous")) "response" else as.character(fit$q.set) .reference <- setdiff(as.character(fit$y.levels), .labels) # An ordinal component is a cumulative logit at its threshold, but boostmtree's # documentation does not say which side of the threshold it models, so the # label names the threshold only. (Its 2.0.2 source codes P(y <= k); read the # installed package before relying on that.) .components <- switch(fit$family,   continuous = .response,   binary = ,   nominal = paste(.response, "=", .labels, "against", paste(.reference, collapse = ", ")),   ordinal = paste(.response, "threshold", .labels) ) fit_summary <- data.frame(   component = .components,   best_m = as.integer(fit$m.opt),   cv_error = mapply(function(e, m) e[m, "l2"], .err, fit$m.opt) ) knitr::kable(fit_summary, col.names = c("Response component", "Best M (cross-validated)",                                         "Cross-validated error there (standardized)")) # The cross-validated error by iteration, and the fitted rho, phi and lambda. # Best M at the right edge means M was too small. p_error <- plot(gg_boost_error(fit)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(p_error, "nb-boostmtree-error") p_error # Free size: three stacked panels, one per parameter. p_path <- plot(gg_boost_path(fit)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(p_path, "nb-boostmtree-path", height = 8) p_path # Observed against fitted values over follow-up, in time bins. # The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the shapes from the legend. p_calibration <- plot(gg_boost_calibration(fit)) +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text()) save_figure(p_calibration, "nb-boostmtree-calibration") p_calibration # Importance of each predictor's main effect and its interaction with time; the # interaction is where a predictor whose effect changes over follow-up shows. # vimp.boostmtree() permutes each predictor at random, so it is seeded and # cached like the fit. Unseeded, the importances moved from render to render, # and with them the six variables the effects below are drawn for. vimp <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree-vimp", vimp.boostmtree(fit), seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) # Free size: one row per predictor, and one panel per effect, at the 6.5 in page width. p_vimp <- plot(gg_boost_vimp(vimp)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(p_vimp, "nb-boostmtree-importance", width = 6.5, height = 7) p_vimp # unnumbered: each child chunk below carries its own label and caption # Partial effects over time, for EFFECT_VARIABLES or the six most important. # An ordinal or nominal fit reports importance once per response component, so # a variable is ranked by its largest importance across them. .vimp_main <- gg_boost_vimp(vimp, components = "main") .top <- sort(tapply(.vimp_main$importance, as.character(.vimp_main$variable), max), decreasing = TRUE) .effect_vars <- if (is.null(EFFECT_VARIABLES)) head(names(.top), 6L) else EFFECT_VARIABLES .unknown <- setdiff(.effect_vars, .predictors) if (length(.unknown)) stop("EFFECT_VARIABLES names no predictor: ", paste(.unknown, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE) # One partial.plot() covers every response component: ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 and # later take an ordinal or nominal one whole and facet its figure by component. # Each component is renamed as the fit summary names it, not by its bare level. .fence <- strrep("`", 3) .seen <- new.env() .child <- function(label, caption, code, opts = NULL) {   label <- gsub("(^-+|-+$)", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(label)))   if (!is.null(.seen[[label]])) stop("Two outputs would share the label ", label, ".", call. = FALSE)   .seen[[label]] <- TRUE   .opt <- paste0("#| ", sub("-.*$", "", label), "-cap: ", encodeString(caption, quote = """))   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(paste0(.fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: ", label), .opt, opts, code, .fence),                         envir = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "
")   cat("
") } # partial.plot() is the slowest step after the fit: one prediction over every # patient per grid value, 25 values per continuous covariate. It is cached # beside the fit and keyed on it, so a re-render that changes only prose skips # it, and a refit or a changed EFFECT_VARIABLES stops until REFIT, as the fit does. .partial <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree-partial",                       partial.plot(fit, x.var.names = .effect_vars, output = "data", verbose = FALSE,                                    progress = get(".job")$progress("prediction")),                       seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) .effect <- gg_boost_effect(.partial) .relabel <- .components[match(levels(.effect$response), .labels)] # A component ggBoostedTrees names differently from the fit would otherwise be # drawn under a blank label; stop and say so instead. if (anyNA(.relabel)) {   stop("ggBoostedTrees labels a response component this job does not recognize: ",        paste(levels(.effect$response)[is.na(.relabel)], collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } levels(.effect$response) <- .relabel # What ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 still cannot do: a continuous covariate is drawn as # a curve and a factor as a point per level, on axes ggplot2 cannot share, so # plot() refuses an effect holding both. Each kind is drawn in its own figure, # which is why p_effects is a list. .discrete <- tapply(!is.na(.effect$x_label), .effect$variable, any) .discrete <- .discrete[!is.na(.discrete)] .parts <- split(names(.discrete), .discrete) .kinds <- ifelse(names(.parts) == "TRUE", "categorical", "continuous") # Free size, paged: one facet per predictor, two by two on a page no larger than # 6.5 by 9 in. With several response components ggBoostedTrees draws one column # per predictor and one row per component, so a page holds two predictors. .n_components <- nlevels(.effect$response) .pages <- lapply(unname(.parts), function(v) {   if (.n_components > 1L) {     hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), panel_height = 3 * .n_components, page_height = 3 * .n_components)   } else {     hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), page_height = 6)   } }) # One plot per page, kind by kind: p_effects holds every page, and .effect_page says which kind and page each is. p_effects <- list() .effect_page <- list() for (.k in seq_along(.parts)) {   for (.j in seq_along(.pages[[.k]])) {     part <- .effect[.effect$variable %in% .parts[[.k]][.pages[[.k]][[.j]]$index], , drop = FALSE]     part$variable <- droplevels(part$variable)     # The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the time colors from the legend.     p_effects[[length(p_effects) + 1L]] <- plot(part) +       hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())     .effect_page[[length(.effect_page) + 1L]] <- list(kind = .kinds[[.k]], page = .j, of = length(.pages[[.k]]),                                                       size = .pages[[.k]][[.j]], vars = levels(part$variable))   } } .key <- c(continuous = paste("Each solid line is the effect at one follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",                              "time as in the color bar."),           categorical = paste("Each point is the effect at one level and follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",                               "time as in the color bar.")) for (.i in seq_along(p_effects)) {   .p <- p_effects[[.i]]   .pg <- .effect_page[[.i]]   save_figure(.p, sprintf("nb-boostmtree-effects-%s-page-%02d", .pg$kind, .pg$page),               width = .pg$size$width, height = .pg$size$height)   .on_page <- if (.pg$of > 1L) paste0(" Page ", .pg$page, " of ", .pg$of, ": ", paste(.pg$vars, collapse = ", "), ".") else ""   .child(paste("fig effects", .pg$kind, .pg$page),          paste0("Partial effects over follow-up, ", .pg$kind, " predictors, one panel per predictor. ", .key[[.pg$kind]],                 .on_page),          ".p", opts = c(sprintf("#| fig-width: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(.pg$size$width)),                         sprintf("#| fig-height: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(.pg$size$height)))) } .p .p # Fitted trajectories for a sample of patients, with their observed values as # points, and the cohort's mean fitted value over time drawn across them. The # patients are labeled by digest, so none is identified. traces <- gg_boost_trajectory(fit) # Visit times are irregular, so most exact times belong to one patient, and a # mean taken at each time would join single values. The mean is taken instead # within ten equal-count time bins, over every patient's fitted values, and # drawn at each bin's mean time. A bin is per response component when there # are several. .edges <- unique(stats::quantile(traces$time, seq(0, 1, length.out = 11L), names = FALSE)) # plot() reports that it chose the patients at random; SEED makes the choice # the same on every render. p_traces <- withr::with_seed(SEED, plot(traces, n_max = N_TRACES)) + ggplot2::labs(x = .time, y = .response) +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) Drawing 100 of 300 subjects, chosen at random. Pass n_max = Inf to draw all, or subset to choose; call set.seed() first for a reproducible sample. if (length(.edges) < 2L) {   # Every visit at one time leaves no span to bin, and no line to draw.   trace_means <- NULL   cat("Every visit is at one time, so no mean line is drawn.
") } else {   traces$.bin <- cut(traces$time, .edges, include.lowest = TRUE)   .by <- intersect(c("response", ".bin"), names(traces))   trace_means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(traces, traces[.by], drop = TRUE), function(b) {     data.frame(b[1L, setdiff(.by, ".bin"), drop = FALSE], time = mean(b$time), fitted = mean(b$fitted),                n_patients = length(unique(b$id)))   }))   p_traces <- p_traces +     ggplot2::geom_line(data = trace_means, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[["time"]], y = .data[["fitted"]]),                        linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) } save_figure(p_traces, "nb-boostmtree-traces") p_traces # The product of this job. It is separate from the cache on purpose: the cache # is this job's internals and this file its interface, which carries the # selection a later job would rebuild the rows from. fit <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(   fit,   data = .provenance_data,   analysis = list(response = .response, time = .time, family = FAMILY, M = M, nu = NU),   cohort = list(n_patients = length(unique(.patient)), n_visits = nrow(d)),   selection = attr(job_data$record, "selection") ) saveRDS(fit, set_path("estimates", "nb-boostmtree.rds"))
