code: # Demo: the fit's selection is used; set any of these only to confirm it. # NULL takes the value the fit job used. WHERE <- NULL ID <- NULL KEY <- NULL  # Demo: how many variables get dependence plots, ranked by VIMP. The partials # are the expensive step, so keep this small. # With BANDS_B above 0, a bigger TOP_K computes bands only for the new variables, but # still regrows all BANDS_B subsample forests to do it. TOP_K <- 4  # Demo: or name the variables yourself. NULL takes the top TOP_K by VIMP. PARTIAL_VARS <- NULL  # Demo: seed for VIMP and the partials. It is part of every cache key. # cache_fit() seeds R's generator with it before each call, and vimp() is also # handed it as `seed =`, negated as randomForestSRC documents. SEED <- 2026  # Demo: subsample forests for the confidence intervals on importance and the # bands on the partial plots. 0 draws neither. #   25-50 for a first look at a draft; the bands are rough but show their shape. #   100 for a report. It is randomForestSRC's default, and enough because the #   intervals are estimate +/- 1.96 SE: they need a stable SE, not stable tail #   percentiles, which would take several hundred. #   200 or more only for 99% intervals, or when a rerun with another SEED moves #   the band edges by more than you would accept in a figure. # Cost is about BANDS_B x SUBRATIO fits of the full forest. Submit the job to # compute them; job_status() shows how many forests are grown and the time left. BANDS_B <- 0  # Demo: fraction of patients in each subsample. NULL takes randomForestSRC's # default, exp(-1) (0.37) up to 1000 patients and exp(-1) * sqrt(1000 / n) above, # so a larger cohort gets a smaller fraction. Leave it NULL unless the check # below warns. #   Raise it when a subsample would hold too few of the smallest class: the job #   warns below 100. Small subsamples grow shallow #   forests whose curves are flatter than the full forest's. #   Keep it at or below 0.5. Subsampling estimates the spread only while each #   subsample is a small part of the cohort; near 1 every subsample forest is #   nearly the full forest, and the bands shrink to the forest's own tree-to-tree #   noise, far narrower than the real uncertainty. SUBRATIO <- NULL  # Demo: how the partial plots draw their bands. "ribbon" shades a band around # each continuous curve; "bars" draws an error bar at each grid point instead, # which reads better in black and white. Categorical predictors always get error bars. BAND_STYLE <- "ribbon"  # Demo: with BAND_STYLE <- "bars", where to draw the bars, as a named list of # values per continuous predictor, e.g. list(age = c(50, 60, 70, 80), lvef = c(30, 50)). # NULL, or a predictor left out, draws a bar at every grid point. The values # must lie inside the range of the predictor's partial plot, which can be # narrower than its observed range; the job stops before growing anything if one # does not. Changing them only redraws: each subsample curve is read off at # these values the way the plotted line is drawn, straight between grid points, # so no forest is regrown. BAND_AT <- NULL  # Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the # render instead of returning the old result; TRUE recomputes only the caches # that are out of date. REFIT <- FALSE  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

code: .handoff <- set_path("estimates", "rfc.rds") if (!file.exists(.handoff)) {   stop("No forest at ", .handoff, ". Render the rfc-fit job in this set first; ",        "this job explains that forest and never grows its own.", call. = FALSE) } .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) .forest_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.handoff, "forest", .cfg, "the rfc-fit job") forest <- .forest_read$value .provenance_data <- .forest_read$lineage$data .provenance_artifacts <- c(.forest_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.forest_read$record)) if (!identical(forest$family, "class")) {   stop("rfc.rds holds a '", forest$family, "' forest, not a classification forest.", call. = FALSE) } CACHE_DIR <- dirname(.handoff) # This job reads no data: the forest carries its training rows. The fit job # recorded how it chose them, and a setting above that differs from the fit's # stops here rather than describe rows the forest was not grown on. .sel <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(   .cfg, .forest_read$lineage, list(where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY), read = FALSE, source = "rfc.rds" )$selection knitr::kable(data.frame(step = c("ID", "KEY", "WHERE", "Rows"),                         value = c(.sel$id, paste(.sel$key, collapse = ", "),                                   if (length(.sel$where_shown)) paste(.sel$where_shown, collapse = "; ") else "none",                                   .sel$rows)),              col.names = c("Data", ""))

code: vi <- cache_fit("rfc-vimp", vimp(forest, seed = -abs(SEED)), seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) # Free size: one row per predictor, and one panel per class, at the 6.5 in page width # drawn half as large again in the report. # The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the colors from the legend. .fig <- plot(gg_vimp(vi)) +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text()) save_figure(.fig, "rfc-explain-importance", width = 6.5, height = 7) .fig # A classification forest reports importance per class as well as overall; # the ranking uses the overall column, so no variable is counted twice. # # Minimal depth ranks by how near the root a variable first splits, a second # opinion that needs no VIMP calculation. Cheap, so not cached. imp <- vi$importance[, "all"] ranked <- names(sort(imp, decreasing = TRUE)) depth <- max.subtree(forest)$order[, 1] data.frame(variable = ranked,            vimp = round(imp[ranked], 4),            min_depth = round(depth[ranked], 2),            row.names = NULL) variable    vimp min_depth 1 creat_pr  0.1417      2.11 2     lvef  0.0675      1.57 3   hx_chf  0.0406      1.57 4      age  0.0313      1.49 5 plvmassi  0.0144      2.17 6    hx_dm  0.0057      3.91 7      bmi  0.0050      2.69 8   female -0.0027      4.12 9  nyha_pr -0.0112      3.02 if (is.null(PARTIAL_VARS)) {   sel <- head(ranked, TOP_K) } else {   # A misspelt name would otherwise fail deep inside the partial call, or be   # dropped from a plot without a word.   .unknown <- setdiff(PARTIAL_VARS, forest$xvar.names)   if (length(.unknown)) {     stop("PARTIAL_VARS names variable(s) the forest was not grown on: ",          paste(.unknown, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)   }   sel <- PARTIAL_VARS } # Each dependence figure is drawn a page at a time, panels in a grid no larger # than the printed page (6.5 by 9 in), and each page is a child chunk of its # own so Quarto numbers it, as dc-eda's pages are. A study's TOP_K or # PARTIAL_VARS sets how many pages there are; nothing here refuses a count. .fence <- strrep("`", 3) .page_child <- function(kind, i, pages, vars, caption) {   page <- pages[[i]]   if (length(pages) > 1L) {     caption <- paste0(caption, " Page ", i, " of ", length(pages), ": ",                       paste(vars[page$index], collapse = ", "), ".")   }   code <- c(paste0(.fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: fig-", kind, "-", i),             paste0("#| fig-cap: ", encodeString(caption, quote = "\"")),             sprintf("#| fig-width: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(page$width)),             sprintf("#| fig-height: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(page$height)), ".fig", .fence)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = code, envir = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")   cat("\n") }

code: # Demo: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset). DATASET <- "built"  # Demo: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset. ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL  # Demo: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row: #   WHERE <- quote(age >= 18) #   WHERE <- rlang::exprs(age >= 18, hx_chf == 1) WHERE <- NULL  # Demo: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN; # name another column, such as "randid", if the study uses one. ID <- "patient_id"  # Demo: what makes a row unique; one row per patient unless repeated measures # add their visit time or date, for example KEY <- c(ID, "iv_echo"). KEY <- ID  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one # registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key; #     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last", #     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column #     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE" #     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record #     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq") #     breaks it. This job models one row per #     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  # Demo: the outcome to classify. Any coding works: 0/1, "yes"/"no" or a label. # The read step makes it a factor, which is what makes this a classification # forest rather than a regression on the codes. RESPONSE <- "complication"  # Demo: the class whose one-versus-rest ROC curve and AUC this report should # show. Use its label after RESPONSE becomes a factor: "1" for a 0/1 outcome, # "yes" for no/yes, or the clinical category of interest for multiclass data. ROC_CLASS <- "1"  # Demo: the candidate predictors. Name them rather than taking every column: a # built dataset carries identifiers, dates and derived outcomes, and a forest # will split on a date that quietly encodes follow-up. PREDICTORS <- c("age", "female", "bmi", "hx_chf", "hx_dm", "nyha_pr", "lvef", "plvmassi", "creat_pr")  # Demo: forest size and seed. The error-by-trees plot below says whether NTREE # was enough: a curve still falling at its right edge was not. SEED makes the # forest reproducible and is part of its cache key. It is used twice, on # purpose: cache_fit() seeds R's generator with it, and rfsrc() is handed it # as `seed =`, negated as randomForestSRC documents. Without that # argument rfsrc() draws a seed from R's generator, so the forest would depend # on whatever ran before it. NTREE <- 300 SEED  <- 2026  # Demo: "na.omit" drops a patient missing any predictor; "na.impute" keeps them # and imputes inside the forest. The classification and regression exemplars # imputed. Dropping is simpler to report and can shrink the cohort a great deal. NA_ACTION <- "na.impute"  # Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the # render instead of returning the old forest; TRUE recomputes only the caches # that are out of date, so it is safe to leave on while iterating. REFIT <- FALSE  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

code: # The checksum of every dataset in manifest.yaml is checked before anything is # read, so a result can name the data that produced it. It stops on a mismatch. hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,                                           where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,                                           reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY, one_row_per_patient = TRUE) d <- job_data$data .provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) .outcomes <- intersect(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS) if (length(.outcomes)) {   stop("Do not include the outcome variable in PREDICTORS: ", .outcomes, ".", call. = FALSE) } .duplicated <- unique(PREDICTORS[duplicated(PREDICTORS)]) if (length(.duplicated)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a variable more than once: ", paste(.duplicated, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } # A forest must not be trained on an identifier. It would split on who a # patient is, not on what is true of them, and the saved forest keeps its # training columns, so the identifier would be written into rfc.rds. .selection <- attr(job_data$record, "selection") .identifiers <- PREDICTORS[tolower(PREDICTORS) %in% tolower(c(.selection$id, .selection$key))] if (length(.identifiers)) {   stop("Do not include the patient identifier or a KEY column in PREDICTORS: ",        paste(.identifiers, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } # Nor may the identifier be the outcome: the forest keeps its outcome column # too. A KEY column that is not the ID, a visit time say, may be one. if (any(tolower(RESPONSE) == tolower(.selection$id))) {   stop("The patient identifier (", .selection$id, ") cannot be an outcome of this job.", call. = FALSE) } .missing <- setdiff(c(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS), names(d)) if (length(.missing)) {   stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE) } d <- d[, c(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS), drop = FALSE]  # A forest cannot learn from a patient with no outcome, and na.impute would # impute one. So the outcome is required whatever NA_ACTION says. .no_outcome <- is.na(d[[RESPONSE]]) if (any(.no_outcome)) {   stop(sum(.no_outcome), " patient(s) have no ", RESPONSE, ". Resolve them in the ",        "dataset build; the forest will not.", call. = FALSE) }  # A numeric 0/1 outcome grows a REGRESSION forest, whose "probabilities" can # fall outside 0 and 1 and whose error is a mean squared error. Nothing warns. d[[RESPONSE]] <- factor(d[[RESPONSE]]) if (!is.character(ROC_CLASS) || length(ROC_CLASS) != 1L || is.na(ROC_CLASS) || !nzchar(ROC_CLASS) ||       !ROC_CLASS %in% levels(d[[RESPONSE]])) {   stop("ROC_CLASS must name one observed level of ", RESPONSE, "; ", deparse(ROC_CLASS),        " is not an observed level. Choose one of: ", paste(levels(d[[RESPONSE]]), collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } ROC_OUTCOME <- match(ROC_CLASS, levels(d[[RESPONSE]]))  # A forest splits a text column only as a factor, so text predictors are # converted here, and named, rather than left for the fit to refuse or coerce. .chr <- PREDICTORS[vapply(d[PREDICTORS], is.character, logical(1L))] if (length(.chr)) {   d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor)   cat("Text predictors converted to factors: ", paste(.chr, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "") } # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption if (!is.null(job_data$attrition)) {   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-data-attrition",     paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(paste0("Analysis set `", ANALYSIS_SET, "`: exclusions, in order"), quote = "\"")),     "knitr::kable(job_data$attrition)", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n") } # na.omit drops a patient missing any predictor and na.impute keeps them, so the # cohort the forest is grown on is said here, before it is. # randomForestSRC discards a predictor with no values at all and keeps every # row, so such a column would leave the forest without a word and the table # below would count every row as dropped. Stop on it instead. .empty <- PREDICTORS[vapply(d[PREDICTORS], function(x) all(is.na(x)), logical(1L))] if (length(.empty)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a column with no values: ", paste(.empty, collapse = ", "),        ". Remove it from PREDICTORS.", call. = FALSE) } .na_handling <- if (NA_ACTION == "na.impute") "impute" else "drop" .missing_values <- hvtiRtemplates:::.missing_cases(d, RESPONSE = RESPONSE, PREDICTORS = PREDICTORS, action = .na_handling) knitr::kable(.missing_values)

The partials # are the expensive step, so keep this small. # With BANDS_B above 0, a bigger TOP_K computes bands only for the new variables, but # still regrows all BANDS_B subsample forests to do it. TOP_K <- 4  # Demo: or name the variables yourself. NULL takes the top TOP_K by VIMP. PARTIAL_VARS <- NULL  # Demo: seed for VIMP and the partials. SEED <- 2026  # Demo: subsample forests for the confidence intervals on importance and the # bands on the partial plots. 0 draws neither. #   25-50 for a first look at a draft; the bands are rough but show their shape. #   100 for a report. It is randomForestSRC's default, and enough because the #   intervals are estimate +/- 1.96 SE: they need a stable SE, not stable tail #   percentiles, which would take several hundred. #   200 or more only for 99% intervals, or when a rerun with another SEED moves #   the band edges by more than you would accept in a figure. # Cost is about BANDS_B x SUBRATIO fits of the full forest. Submit the job to # compute them; job_status() shows how many forests are grown and the time left. BANDS_B <- 0  # Demo: fraction of patients in each subsample. NULL takes randomForestSRC's # default, exp(-1) (0.37) up to 1000 patients and exp(-1) * sqrt(1000 / n) above, # so a larger cohort gets a smaller fraction. Leave it NULL unless you have a # reason to change it. #   Small subsamples grow shallow forests whose curves are flatter than the full #   forest's. #   Keep it at or below 0.5. Subsampling estimates the spread only while each #   subsample is a small part of the cohort; near 1 every subsample forest is #   nearly the full forest, and the bands shrink to the forest's own tree-to-tree #   noise, far narrower than the real uncertainty. SUBRATIO <- NULL  # Demo: how the partial plots draw their bands. The values # must lie inside the range of the predictor's partial plot, which can be # narrower than its observed range; the job stops before growing anything if one # does not. KEY <- ID  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one # registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key; #     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last", #     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column #     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE" #     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record #     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq") #     breaks it. This job models one row per #     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  # Demo: the continuous outcome. Transform it first if its distribution calls # for it (a length of stay is usually logged); the forest predicts on the # scale given here. RESPONSE <- "log_los"  # Demo: the candidate predictors. Name them rather than taking every column: a # built dataset carries identifiers, dates and derived outcomes, and a forest # will split on a date that quietly encodes follow-up. PREDICTORS <- c("age", "female", "bmi", "hx_chf", "hx_dm", "nyha_pr", "lvef", "plvmassi", "creat_pr")  # Demo: forest size and seed. The error-by-trees plot below says whether NTREE # was enough: a curve still falling at its right edge was not. SEED makes the # forest reproducible and is part of its cache key. It is used twice, on # purpose: cache_fit() seeds R's generator with it, and rfsrc() is handed it # as `seed =`, negated as randomForestSRC documents. Without that # argument rfsrc() draws a seed from R's generator, so the forest would depend # on whatever ran before it. NTREE <- 300 SEED  <- 2026  # Demo: "na.omit" drops a patient missing any predictor; "na.impute" keeps them # and imputes inside the forest. The classification and regression exemplars # imputed. Dropping is simpler to report and can shrink the cohort a great deal. NA_ACTION <- "na.impute"  # Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the # render instead of returning the old forest; TRUE recomputes only the caches # that are out of date, so it is safe to leave on while iterating. REFIT <- FALSE  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

code: # The checksum of every dataset in manifest.yaml is checked before anything is # read, so a result can name the data that produced it. It stops on a mismatch. hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,                                           where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,                                           reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY, one_row_per_patient = TRUE) d <- job_data$data .provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) .outcomes <- intersect(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS) if (length(.outcomes)) {   stop("Do not include the outcome variable in PREDICTORS: ", .outcomes, ".", call. = FALSE) } .duplicated <- unique(PREDICTORS[duplicated(PREDICTORS)]) if (length(.duplicated)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a variable more than once: ", paste(.duplicated, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } # A forest must not be trained on an identifier. It would split on who a # patient is, not on what is true of them, and the saved forest keeps its # training columns, so the identifier would be written into rfr.rds. .selection <- attr(job_data$record, "selection") .identifiers <- PREDICTORS[tolower(PREDICTORS) %in% tolower(c(.selection$id, .selection$key))] if (length(.identifiers)) {   stop("Do not include the patient identifier or a KEY column in PREDICTORS: ",        paste(.identifiers, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } # Nor may the identifier be the outcome: the forest keeps its outcome column # too. A KEY column that is not the ID, a visit time say, may be one. if (any(tolower(RESPONSE) == tolower(.selection$id))) {   stop("The patient identifier (", .selection$id, ") cannot be an outcome of this job.", call. = FALSE) } .missing <- setdiff(c(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS), names(d)) if (length(.missing)) {   stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE) } d <- d[, c(RESPONSE, PREDICTORS), drop = FALSE]  # A forest cannot learn from a patient with no outcome, and na.impute would # impute one. So the outcome is required whatever NA_ACTION says. .no_outcome <- is.na(d[[RESPONSE]]) if (any(.no_outcome)) {   stop(sum(.no_outcome), " patient(s) have no ", RESPONSE, ". Resolve them in the ",        "dataset build; the forest will not.", call. = FALSE) }  # A factor or character outcome grows a CLASSIFICATION forest, one class per # distinct value. Nothing warns. if (!is.numeric(d[[RESPONSE]])) {   stop(RESPONSE, " must be numeric for a regression forest; it is ",        class(d[[RESPONSE]])[1L], ".", call. = FALSE) }  # A forest splits a text column only as a factor, so text predictors are # converted here, and named, rather than left for the fit to refuse or coerce. .chr <- PREDICTORS[vapply(d[PREDICTORS], is.character, logical(1L))] if (length(.chr)) {   d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor)   cat("Text predictors converted to factors: ", paste(.chr, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "") } # unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption if (!is.null(job_data$attrition)) {   .fence <- strrep("`", 3)   cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(     paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-data-attrition",     paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(paste0("Analysis set `", ANALYSIS_SET, "`: exclusions, in order"), quote = "\"")),     "knitr::kable(job_data$attrition)", .fence   ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n") } # na.omit drops a patient missing any predictor and na.impute keeps them, so the # cohort the forest is grown on is said here, before it is. # randomForestSRC discards a predictor with no values at all and keeps every # row, so such a column would leave the forest without a word and the table # below would count every row as dropped. Stop on it instead. .empty <- PREDICTORS[vapply(d[PREDICTORS], function(x) all(is.na(x)), logical(1L))] if (length(.empty)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a column with no values: ", paste(.empty, collapse = ", "),        ". Remove it from PREDICTORS.", call. = FALSE) } .na_handling <- if (NA_ACTION == "na.impute") "impute" else "drop" .missing_values <- hvtiRtemplates:::.missing_cases(d, RESPONSE = RESPONSE, PREDICTORS = PREDICTORS, action = .na_handling) knitr::kable(.missing_values)

SEED <- 2026  # Demo: subsample forests for the confidence intervals on importance and the # bands on the partial plots. 0 draws neither. #   25-50 for a first look at a draft; the bands are rough but show their shape. #   100 for a report. code: # Demo: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset). # It can be the counting-process rows themselves, or the one-row cohort with # the rows named in JOIN below. DATASET <- "intervals"  # Demo: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset. WHERE # below is checked to keep a patient whole; an analysis set is not, so one that # selects intervals rather than patients would shorten follow-up unchecked. ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL  # Demo: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row. A # condition must keep or drop a patient whole, so name a column whose value is # the same on every row of a patient, such as age at listing. A condition on a # time-varying column would cut follow-up short, and stops the render. WHERE <- NULL  # Demo: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN. ID <- "patient_id"  # Demo: each interval's start and stop, and its event, coded 1 when the event # ends that interval and 0 otherwise. Only a patient's last interval can carry # an event. Code a competing event 0: it censors. START <- "start" STOP  <- "stop" EVENT <- "event"  # Demo: what makes a row unique: the patient and the start of the interval. KEY <- c(ID, START)  # Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads DATASET alone. When DATASET is the # one-row cohort, name the registered counting-process dataset here and leave # REDUCE NULL, so each joined record is one interval of a patient's follow-up. # The cohort decides the patients; the joined records of other patients are # dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all, #     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs, #     such as the baseline predictors. #   REDUCE: keeps one record per patient, which this job does not want. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL  # Demo: the candidate predictors, baseline and time-varying alike. Name them # rather than taking every column: a dataset carries identifiers, dates and # derived outcomes, and a forest will split on a date that encodes follow-up. PREDICTORS <- c("xtd", "x_1", "x_2", "x_3")  # Demo: forest size and seed. SEED makes the forest reproducible and is part of # its cache key. It is used three times, on purpose: cache_fit() seeds R's # generator with it, rhf() is handed it as `seed =`, negated as randomForestRHF # documents, and tune.treesize.rhf() is handed its absolute value. NTREE <- 300 SEED  <- 2026  # Demo: the number of terminal nodes in each tree. NULL chooses it by # out-of-bag risk with tune.treesize.rhf(), and the figure below shows the # search. Tree size is the setting a hazard forest is most sensitive to, which # is why this template tunes it where the rfs templates tune nothing; a number # skips the search, which is slow on a large study. TREESIZE <- NULL  # Needs no edit unless the dataset has a defect. Repairs this job makes to the # counting-process rows while the dataset fix is in flight; each one marks the # report a draft, and a final render refuses it, because the rows a final # result rests on come from the dataset, so every job in the study agrees. #   "clip"    clips an interval that starts before the one before it ends back #             to that end, and drops an interval left empty #   "drop_na" drops intervals missing a predictor REPAIR <- character()  # Demo: caps on predictors with implausible tails, as c(column = cap), or NULL for # none. CAPS <- NULL  # Demo: the look-ahead check, a screen for timing problems, not proof of one. # randomForestRHF assumes each interval's predictors were known when it began, # and cannot tell when they were not. The names # are the file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

The ID is # matched to a plain integer because duplicated() on an integer64 ignores fromLast. .pt <- match(d[[.selection$id]], unique(d[[.selection$id]])) .final <- which(!duplicated(.pt, fromLast = TRUE) & c(FALSE, .pt[-1L] == .pt[-length(.pt)])) if (!is.null(LOOKAHEAD_INTERVAL)) {   .final <- .final[abs(d[[STOP]][.final] - d[[START]][.final] - LOOKAHEAD_INTERVAL) < LOOKAHEAD_INTERVAL / 25] } .changed <- matrix(vapply(PREDICTORS, function(p) d[[p]][.final] != d[[p]][.final - 1L], logical(length(.final))),                    ncol = length(PREDICTORS), dimnames = list(NULL, PREDICTORS)) .is_event <- d[[EVENT]][.final] == 1 .lookahead <- data.frame(final = c("Event", "No event"),                          checked = c(sum(.is_event), sum(!.is_event)),                          changed = c(sum(rowSums(.changed[.is_event, , drop = FALSE]) > 0),                                      sum(rowSums(.changed[!.is_event, , drop = FALSE]) > 0))) .on_events <- sort(colSums(.changed[.is_event, , drop = FALSE]), decreasing = TRUE) .on_events <- .on_events[.on_events > 0] if (length(.on_events)) {   cat("Changing most often on an event's final interval: ",       paste0(names(utils::head(.on_events, 5L)), " (", utils::head(.on_events, 5L), ")", collapse = ", "), "
", sep = "") } Changing most often on an event's final interval: xtd (124) if (LOOKAHEAD == "reset" && length(.final)) {   d[.final, PREDICTORS] <- d[.final - 1L, PREDICTORS]   cat(length(.final), " final intervals given the predictors of the interval before (LOOKAHEAD = "reset").
", sep = "") } knitr::kable(.lookahead, col.names = c("Final interval", "Checked", "A predictor changes"))

CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "rhf.rds")) # rhf() needs each row's patient, and a saved forest keeps its data, so the # study's identifiers would be written into rhf.rds. Each patient is numbered # 1 to n instead, in the order of the rows: the forest can still tell one # patient's intervals from another's, and no study identifier is stored. .fit_data <- data.frame(id = match(d[[.selection$id]], unique(d[[.selection$id]])),                         start = d[[START]], stop = d[[STOP]], event = d[[EVENT]], d[PREDICTORS]) # Surv is written bare on purpose. randomForestRHF reads the call's head by name and # refuses survival::Surv(), and it finds Surv itself, so survival need not be attached. model <- Surv(id, start, stop, event) ~ . # The saved forest keeps this formula, and a formula keeps the environment it # was made in; set it, so a job run anywhere else does not write every object # beside the formula, `job_data` and its patient IDs included, into the forest. environment(model) <- globalenv() # Each cache holds the forest and so every interval it was grown on: written # owner-only from the start, and set so if an older cache is already there. .cache_files <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, c("rhf-treesize.rds", "rhf-forest.rds")) # Hours at study size. Started from the console it dies with the session, so an # uncached fit is refused there: run the job with hvtiRtemplates::submit_job(). hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("rhf-forest", dir = CACHE_DIR,                                why = "a hazard forest on every interval of follow-up takes hours at study size",                                refit = REFIT) if (is.null(TREESIZE)) {   hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("rhf-treesize", dir = CACHE_DIR,                                  why = "the tree-size search grows a forest at each size it tries",                                  refit = REFIT)   tuned <- hvtiRtemplates:::.owner_only(.cache_files, cache_fit(     "rhf-treesize",     tune.treesize.rhf(model, .fit_data, ntree = NTREE, perf = "risk", seed = abs(SEED), verbose = FALSE,                       forest = FALSE),     seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT   ))   .treesize <- tuned$best.size } else {   tuned <- NULL   .treesize <- TREESIZE } forest <- hvtiRtemplates:::.owner_only(.cache_files, cache_fit(   "rhf-forest",   rhf(model, data = .fit_data, ntree = NTREE, treesize = .treesize, seed = -abs(SEED)),   seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT )) forest Number of records: 471           Sample size (unique IDs): 150             Average records per ID: 3.14            Number of deaths/events: 127                    Number of trees: 300         Average tree size (leaves): 5                  Average node size: 59.602   No. features tried at each split: 2    Total no. time-varying features: 1                 Total no. features: 4                             Family: surv-tdc                          Splitrule: hazard.loglik *random*               No. of random splits: 10                           OOB risk: -1.524                       TDC analysis: YES

code: # Demo: the solutions to assign letters and draw in the Sankey, smallest K # first. Letters are carried from each K to the next, so the range must be # consecutive. K_RANGE <- 2:6  # Demo: the solution this study reports, one of K_RANGE. Leave NULL for the # first render: the metrics and sizes below are how K is chosen, and every # section that needs K is skipped, saying so. A final render needs K. A draft # render with K = NULL saves clusters = NULL, so a job that reads this set's # clusters (vt) stops until K is set. K <- 3  # Demo: letters pinned by hand, by solution and PAM cluster number, such as #   OVERRIDES <- list(pm4 = c("1" = "B", "2" = "D", "3" = "C", "4" = "A")) # PAM numbers its clusters arbitrarily, so an override is a domain decision # written down (which cluster a paper calls A), not a fix. Read the cluster # numbers from the sizes table. list() lets the lineage rule choose. Overrides # are keyed on PAM numbers, which sid-fit's forest decides: after a refit they go # stale, so read the sizes table again before reusing them. OVERRIDES <- list()  # Demo: optionally, groups made of clusters at K, such as #   COLLAPSE <- list(Z = c("C", "D", "E")) # written as an extra column G<K>. Letters not named keep their own letter. # NULL writes no group column. COLLAPSE <- NULL  # Demo: a cluster smaller than this at K is flagged. Later per-cluster tables # and a vp-fit with the cluster as outcome need enough patients in each. MIN_SIZE <- 20  # Demo: how far the K metrics run. They are drawn beyond K_RANGE on purpose: an # elbow is only visible with points on both sides of it. K_METRICS_MAX <- 15  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("sid-clusters-sankey"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL # Letters that keep their identity across K. The first solution's clusters # take letters largest first. At each later K, every cluster is the child of # the previous solution's cluster that contributes most of its patients; the # largest child of each parent inherits the parent's letter and its siblings # take fresh ones. An override pins a letter to a PAM cluster number. # PAM numbers its clusters arbitrarily, so nothing here may depend on those # numbers: clusters of equal size are ordered by their first patient (row), # and parents hand out fresh letters in the order of their own letters. sid_align_labels <- function(mat, overrides = list(), pool = LETTERS) {   mat <- as.matrix(mat)   out <- matrix(NA_character_, nrow(mat), ncol(mat), dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(mat)))   pinned <- function(col, ids) {     res <- stats::setNames(rep(NA_character_, length(ids)), as.character(ids))     ov <- overrides[[col]]     if (is.null(ov)) return(res)     bad <- setdiff(names(ov), as.character(ids))     if (length(bad)) {       stop("OVERRIDES$", col, " names unknown cluster id(s): ", toString(bad), call. = FALSE)     }     if (anyDuplicated(ov)) stop("OVERRIDES$", col, " gives one letter to two clusters.", call. = FALSE)     res[names(ov)] <- ov     res   }   fresh <- function(taken) {     l <- setdiff(pool, taken)[1]     if (is.na(l)) stop("Letter pool exhausted: more clusters than letters.", call. = FALSE)     l   }   # Cluster ids of column `x`, largest first, equal sizes by their first row.   by_size <- function(x, ids = unique(x)) {     ids <- as.character(ids)     size <- vapply(ids, function(id) sum(x == id), integer(1))     first <- vapply(ids, function(id) match(id, x), integer(1))     ids[order(-size, first)]   }   used <- character(0)   col1 <- as.character(mat[, 1])   ids <- by_size(col1)   got <- pinned(colnames(mat)[1], ids)   for (id in ids) if (is.na(got[id])) got[id] <- fresh(c(used, got))   used <- unique(c(used, got))   out[, 1] <- got[col1]   for (k in seq_len(ncol(mat))[-1]) {     colk <- as.character(mat[, k])     tab <- table(out[, k - 1], colk)     # rownames(tab) are the previous letters, sorted, so a tie between parents     # goes to the earlier letter whatever PAM's numbering.     parent <- apply(tab, 2, function(col) rownames(tab)[which.max(col)])     got <- pinned(colnames(mat)[k], colnames(tab))     for (p in sort(unique(parent))) {       kids <- by_size(colk, names(parent)[parent == p])       # Checked against the whole column: an override may already have given       # the parent's letter to a cluster of another parent.       if (!p %in% got) {         free <- kids[is.na(got[kids])]         if (length(free)) got[free[1]] <- p       }       for (ch in kids) if (is.na(got[ch])) got[ch] <- fresh(c(used, got))     }     used <- unique(c(used, got))     out[, k] <- got[colk]   }   out }  # Groups made of clusters. A letter not in the map keeps its own letter. sid_collapse <- function(letters, map) {   if (!is.list(map) || is.null(names(map)) || any(is.na(names(map)) | !nzchar(names(map)))) {     stop("COLLAPSE must name each group, such as list(Z = c(\"C\", \"D\"))", call. = FALSE)   }   named <- unlist(map, use.names = FALSE)   twice <- unique(named[duplicated(named)])   if (length(twice)) stop("COLLAPSE has a letter mapped more than once: ", toString(twice), call. = FALSE)   absent <- setdiff(named, letters)   if (length(absent)) stop("COLLAPSE names a letter that is not a cluster at K: ", toString(absent), call. = FALSE)   # A group named for a letter that stays as it is would merge into that cluster.   clash <- intersect(names(map), setdiff(unique(letters), named))   if (length(clash)) {     stop("COLLAPSE has a group name that is also an unmapped cluster at K: ", toString(clash),          ". Rename the group.", call. = FALSE)   }   out <- letters   for (g in names(map)) out[letters %in% map[[g]]] <- g   out }  # cmdscale() returns each axis with an arbitrary sign, so a map can mirror # between renders. Each axis is turned so that the patient furthest from the # origin along it is positive. Among patients equally far, the one whose row # name (the ID digest) sorts first decides, so neither row order nor render # changes the picture. sid_mds_signs <- function(xy) {   key <- if (is.null(rownames(xy))) seq_len(nrow(xy)) else rownames(xy)   for (j in seq_len(ncol(xy))) {     far <- which(abs(xy[, j]) == max(abs(xy[, j])))     if (xy[far[order(key[far])[1]], j] < 0) xy[, j] <- -xy[, j]   }   xy }  # The name a set's clusters are registered under. Dataset names allow only # [a-z0-9_], and SUBJECT and TYPE may themselves hold "_", so the subject's # length is written first: (a_b, c) and (a, b_c) would otherwise share one name. # Names that differ only in case still meet, which the save chunk refuses. sid_dataset_name <- function(subject, type) {   paste0("clusters_", nchar(subject), "_", tolower(subject), "_", tolower(type)) }

Look above for the message ",            "randomForestSRC gave, and check the clustering variables for a constant or near-empty factor.", call. = FALSE)     }     o[c("dist", "outcome.names")]   }, seed = s, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) }) sid_dist <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(sid_fits, `[[`, "dist")) / M # How closely each imputation's distances follow the mean. code: # Half the copies come from categorical variables and half from continuous # ones, as far as each kind allows, so both kinds of column contribute to the # null. An outcome column entered in OUTCOME is a source like any other: a # permuted outcome is as much a null as any other permuted column. # # The kind rule is varpro_coverage()'s: a factor, text or logical column, or a # number with at most 5 distinct values, is categorical. vp_kind <- function(x) {   if (is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) || length(unique(stats::na.omit(x))) <= 5L) {     "categorical"   } else {     "continuous"   } } vp_add_noise <- function(d, predictors, n, seed) {   kinds <- vapply(d[predictors], vp_kind, "")   pools <- split(predictors, kinds)   n_cat <- if (length(pools$categorical) && length(pools$continuous)) {     n %/% 2L   } else if (length(pools$categorical)) {     n   } else {     0L   }   set.seed(abs(seed))   draw <- function(pool, k) if (k == 0L) character() else pool[sample.int(length(pool), k, replace = k > length(pool))]   src <- c(draw(pools$categorical, n_cat), draw(pools$continuous, n - n_cat))   for (i in seq_along(src)) {     set.seed(abs(seed) + i)     d[[paste0("noise", i, "_", src[i])]] <- sample(d[[src[i]]])   }   d } if (NOISE_N < 1) {   stop("NOISE_N must be at least 1: the edge bar needs noise to beat.", call. = FALSE) } if (!(SUBSAMPLE > 0 && SUBSAMPLE < 1)) {   stop("SUBSAMPLE must be a share between 0 and 1 (0.632 draws 63.2% of the patients).", call. = FALSE) } if (REPEATS > 0 && floor(SUBSAMPLE * nrow(d)) < 2) {   stop("SUBSAMPLE of ", nrow(d), " patients leaves fewer than 2 for a refit. Raise SUBSAMPLE or set REPEATS to 0.", call. = FALSE) } # The noise columns are found by the "noise" prefix, so a real variable named # that way would be judged as noise. .noisy <- grep("^noise", .cols, value = TRUE) if (length(.noisy)) {   stop("Variable(s) whose names start with \"noise\", which this job reserves for its noise columns: ",        paste(.noisy, collapse = ", "), ". Rename them in the dataset build.", call. = FALSE) } d_noise <- vp_add_noise(d, .cols, NOISE_N, SEED) # The decisions this job makes from the importance matrix, in one chunk of # their own so they can be checked on a hand-built matrix without a fit. # # varPro splits a factor into one 0/1 column per level and records which # variable each column came from, in attr(fit$x, "xvar.map"). That record is # read, never guessed from the names: a factor f with a level s beside a # numeric fs gets a column named fs.1, which belongs to f, and no rule on the # spelling can tell. vpd_parent <- function(fit) {   map <- attr(fit$x, "xvar.map")   if (is.null(map)) {     stop("This varPro fit records no xvar.map, so its encoded columns cannot be traced to variables. ",          "Update varPro to 3.3.0 or later, set REFIT <- TRUE, and re-render.", call. = FALSE)   }   map } # get.beta.entropy() returns rows only for the variables that formed a # contrast, so the matrix is padded to square, missing entries 0. They are dropped here # instead, and counted, before the fit sees the data. .empty <- PREDICTORS[vapply(d[PREDICTORS], function(x) all(is.na(x)), logical(1L))] if (length(.empty)) {   stop("PREDICTORS names a column with no values: ", paste(.empty, collapse = ", "),        ". Remove it from PREDICTORS.", call. = FALSE) } .missing_values <- hvtiRtemplates:::.missing_cases(d, TIME = TIME, EVENT = EVENT, RESPONSE = RESPONSE,                                                    PREDICTORS = PREDICTORS, action = "drop") d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d), , drop = FALSE] .cohort <- list(n = as.integer(nrow(d))) if (.survival) {   .cohort$n_events <- as.integer(sum(d[[EVENT]] == 1))   .cohort$n_censored <- as.integer(sum(d[[EVENT]] == 0)) } knitr::kable(.missing_values)

# Each noise column is a permuted copy of a real candidate: it keeps that # candidate's values and loses any link to the outcome, so whatever importance # it earns is what chance alone earns. Half the copies come from categorical # candidates and half from continuous ones, as far as each kind allows, # because a variable is judged against noise of its own kind. # # The kind rule is varpro_coverage()'s: a factor, text or logical column, or a # number with at most 5 distinct values, is categorical. vp_kind <- function(x) {   if (is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) || length(unique(stats::na.omit(x))) <= 5L) {     "categorical"   } else {     "continuous"   } } vp_add_noise <- function(d, predictors, n, seed) {   kinds <- vapply(d[predictors], vp_kind, "")   pools <- split(predictors, kinds)   n_cat <- if (length(pools$categorical) && length(pools$continuous)) {     n %/% 2L   } else if (length(pools$categorical)) {     n   } else {     0L   }   set.seed(abs(seed))   draw <- function(pool, k) if (k == 0L) character() else pool[sample.int(length(pool), k, replace = k > length(pool))]   src <- c(draw(pools$categorical, n_cat), draw(pools$continuous, n - n_cat))   for (i in seq_along(src)) {     set.seed(abs(seed) + i)     d[[paste0("noise", i, "_", src[i])]] <- sample(d[[src[i]]])   }   d } if (NOISE_N < 1) {   stop("NOISE_N must be at least 1: the selection rule needs noise to beat.", call. = FALSE) } if (!(SUBSAMPLE > 0 && SUBSAMPLE < 1)) {   stop("SUBSAMPLE must be a share between 0 and 1 (0.632 draws 63.2% of the patients).", call. = FALSE) } if (REPEATS > 0 && floor(SUBSAMPLE * nrow(d)) < 2) {   stop("SUBSAMPLE of ", nrow(d), " patients leaves fewer than 2 for a refit. Raise SUBSAMPLE or set REPEATS to 0.", call. = FALSE) } # The coverage table finds noise by the "noise" prefix, so a real candidate # named that way would be judged as noise. .noisy <- grep("^noise", PREDICTORS, value = TRUE) if (length(.noisy)) {   stop("Candidate(s) whose names start with \"noise\", which this job reserves for its noise columns: ",        paste(.noisy, collapse = ", "), ". Rename them in the dataset build.", call. = FALSE) } d_noise <- vp_add_noise(d, PREDICTORS, NOISE_N, SEED) model <- if (.survival) {   stats::as.formula(paste0("Surv(", TIME, ", ", EVENT, ") ~ .")) } else {   stats::as.formula(paste0(RESPONSE, " ~ .")) } # The saved fit keeps this formula, and a formula keeps the environment it was # made in; set it, so a job run anywhere else does not write every object # beside the formula, `job_data` and its patient IDs included, into vp.rds. environment(model) <- globalenv()

# The selection rule. A real variable is selected when it is tested and its z # beats every TESTED noise column of its kind. varPro's own cutoff (z > 0.79) # does not carry from one fit to another, because z shrinks as more variables # share each tree; noise in the same fit shrinks with it. # # The categorical bar needs care. Categorical noise is rarely tested, and when # it is it almost always scores z = 0 (in the repeats of the screen behind this template: none # tested in 20 of 40, all zero in 18). A bar of 0 lets any tested categorical # variable through, so a categorical bar of 0, or one with no categorical # noise tested, is replaced by the continuous bar. The continuous bar is the # stricter one, since continuous noise picks up split-point bias, so the rule # errs toward missing a real categorical effect rather than admitting a false # one. A continuous bar is never borrowed: when no continuous noise sets a bar # above 0, no continuous variable is selected, because nothing calibrates it. # The table names the bar each variable was judged against. vp_judge <- function(cov) {   # varpro_coverage() brings its own noise_cut and selected; this rule replaces both, so one bar remains.   cov$noise_cut <- NULL   noise <- cov$noise & cov$tested   # A bar is usable only above 0: noise that scores 0 bars nothing.   bar_of <- function(k) {     z <- cov$z[noise & cov$kind == k]     z <- z[!is.na(z)]     if (length(z) && max(z) > 0) max(z) else NA_real_   }   bar_cont <- bar_of("continuous")   bar_cat <- bar_of("categorical")   fallback <- is.na(bar_cat) && !is.na(bar_cont)   if (fallback) bar_cat <- bar_cont   cov$bar <- ifelse(cov$kind == "categorical", bar_cat, bar_cont)   cov$bar_from <- ifelse(cov$kind == "categorical", if (fallback) "continuous (fallback)" else "categorical", "continuous")   cov$bar_from[is.na(cov$bar)] <- "no usable noise bar"   cov$selected <- !cov$noise & cov$tested & (cov$z > cov$bar) %in% TRUE   cov } # cache_fit() writes <dir>/<name>.rds and its default dir is the study's # estimates folder, not this set's, so every call here names the set's. CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "vp.rds")) fit <- cache_fit(   "vp-fit",   varpro(model, d_noise, ntree = NTREE, nvar = NVAR, split.weight = SPLIT_WEIGHT, verbose = FALSE, cores = 1L,          seed = -abs(SEED)),   seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT )

code: # Each refit is cached on its own, so raising REPEATS computes only the new # ones. Redrawing the noise alone would hold the patients fixed and understate # how much the selection moves, so each refit also draws its patients. .stab <- data.frame(r = integer(), variable = character(), selected = logical(), tested = logical()) if (REPEATS > 0) {   .stab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(REPEATS), function(r) {     set.seed(abs(SEED) + r)     rows <- sort(sample.int(nrow(d), floor(SUBSAMPLE * nrow(d))))     dr <- vp_add_noise(d[rows, , drop = FALSE], PREDICTORS, NOISE_N, SEED + r)     fr <- cache_fit(       sprintf("vp-repeat-%02d", r),       varpro(model, dr, ntree = NTREE, nvar = NVAR, split.weight = SPLIT_WEIGHT, verbose = FALSE, cores = 1L,              seed = -abs(SEED + r)),       seed = SEED + r, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT     )     set.seed(abs(SEED) + r)     # As for the full fit: vp_judge() makes the selection, so varpro_coverage()'s empty-noise warning is muffled.     cr <- vp_judge(withCallingHandlers(       ggRandomForests::varpro_coverage(fr, by = "variable", trim = TRIM, noise = "^noise"),       warning = function(w) {         if (grepl("no noise variable was tested", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")       }     ))     cr <- cr[!cr$noise, ]     data.frame(r = r, variable = cr$variable, selected = cr$selected, tested = cr$tested)   }))   .per <- tapply(.stab$selected, .stab$r, sum)   cat("Selected per refit: ", min(.per), " to ", max(.per), " variables.\n", sep = "")   # Over REPEATS, not over the refits a variable appears in: a refit that drops a variable counts against it.   .n_tested <- tapply(.stab$tested, .stab$variable, sum)   .freq <- data.frame(     variable = names(.n_tested),     share_tested = as.vector(.n_tested) / REPEATS,     share_selected = as.vector(tapply(.stab$selected, .stab$variable, sum)[names(.n_tested)]) / REPEATS   )   .freq <- .freq[order(-.freq$share_selected, -.freq$share_tested), ]   knitr::kable(.freq, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE) } else {   cat("Skipped: REPEATS is 0.\n") } Selected per refit: 3 to 5 variables.

code: .handoff <- set_path("estimates", "vp.rds") if (!file.exists(.handoff)) {   stop("No screen at ", .handoff, ". Render the vp-fit job in this set first; ",        "this job explains that screen and never fits its own.", call. = FALSE) } .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) .vp_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.handoff, "screen", .cfg, "the vp-fit job") fit <- .vp_read$value$fit cov <- .vp_read$value$coverage selected <- .vp_read$value$selected .provenance_data <- .vp_read$lineage$data .provenance_artifacts <- c(.vp_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.vp_read$record)) CACHE_DIR <- dirname(.handoff) # This job reads no data: the screen carries its rows. The fit job recorded how # it chose them, and a setting above that differs from the fit's stops here. .sel <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(   .cfg, .vp_read$lineage, list(where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY), read = FALSE, source = "vp.rds" )$selection knitr::kable(data.frame(step = c("ID", "KEY", "WHERE", "Rows"),                         value = c(.sel$id, paste(.sel$key, collapse = ", "),                                   if (length(.sel$where_shown)) paste(.sel$where_shown, collapse = "; ") else "none",                                   .sel$rows)),              col.names = c("Data", "")) # The encoded-column map, read from the fit as vp-dependence reads it. vpi_parent <- function(fit) {   map <- attr(fit$x, "xvar.map")   if (is.null(map)) {     stop("This varPro fit records no xvar.map. Update varPro to 3.3.0 or later and re-render the vp-fit job.", call. = FALSE)   }   map } # One row per processed predictor the screen was given, taken from the map and # not from the gradient table: ivarpro() returns columns only for the # predictors the fit kept, so one cut by split weights or NVAR has no column at # all, and would otherwise vanish from the table instead of being listed. vpi_coverage <- function(grad, parent, screen) {   terms <- names(parent)   have <- terms %in% names(grad)   col_of <- function(t) if (t %in% names(grad)) grad[[t]] else NA_real_   out <- data.frame(     term = terms, variable = unname(parent),     share_na = vapply(terms, function(t) mean(is.na(col_of(t))), numeric(1L)),     median_abs = vapply(terms, function(t) {       g <- col_of(t)       if (all(is.na(g))) NA_real_ else stats::median(abs(g), na.rm = TRUE)     }, numeric(1L)),     row.names = NULL   )   out$gradients <- ifelse(!have, "removed before gradients", ifelse(out$share_na == 1, "none for any patient", "computed"))   m <- match(out$variable, screen$variable)   out$noise <- screen$noise[m] %in% TRUE   out$tested <- screen$tested[m] %in% TRUE   out$selected <- screen$selected[m] %in% TRUE   out$drawn <- out$share_na < 1   out } # The noise reference: the 95th percentile of the noise columns' absolute # gradients, when the rules released any noise column. With guided split # weights they usually did not, and the report says so rather than invent one. vpi_noise_ref <- function(cov, grad = NULL) {   nz <- cov$term[cov$noise & cov$drawn]   if (!length(nz) || is.null(grad)) {     return(list(value = NA_real_, text = "no noise reference: the screen's rules never released a noise column"))   }   v <- stats::quantile(abs(unlist(grad[nz])), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)   list(value = v, text = sprintf("noise reference (95th percentile of |gradient| over %d noise columns): %.3g", length(nz), v)) }

vt_overlap_weights <- function(ps_data, ids, id, arm, arms, score = "prob_t") {   at <- match(ids, as.character(ps_data[[id]]))   e <- ps_data[[score]][at]   ifelse(ps_data[[arm]][at] == arms[1], 1 - e, e) } # Each patient's log relative risk at HORIZON, scaled by its SD, regressed on one # characteristic at a time with overlap weights (Ishwaran and Blackstone, 2025). # The forests are fixed; only patients are resampled. .lr <- r[.eligible & !r$no_arm, c("ID", "log_rr")] .lr_dropped <- sum(!is.finite(.lr$log_rr)) if (.lr_dropped) {   cat(.lr_dropped, " eligible patient(s) have a risk of 0 under an arm, so no relative risk, and are left out of the betas.

",       sep = "") } .bx <- merge(.lr[is.finite(.lr$log_rr), ],              .d_all[c(.vt$settings$id, .vt$predictors$names)], by.x = "ID", by.y = .vt$settings$id) .ps <- .vt$eligibility$ps # Overlap (ATO) weights, computed here: ps_forest()'s own weight column is the # Li-Greene MATCHING weight, which targets a different estimand (ATM). With e # the out-of-bag probability of ARMS[1], a patient on ARMS[1] weighs 1 - e and # one on ARMS[2] weighs e (Li, Morgan and Zaslavsky 2018). .bx$w <- vt_overlap_weights(.ps$data, .bx$ID, .vt$settings$id, .vt$settings$arm, ARMS) # A patient the fit could not score (no predictor observed) has no propensity weight; like a # nonfinite log_rr, they are dropped and counted, never a stop. .no_w <- is.na(.bx$w) if (any(.no_w)) {   cat(sum(.no_w), " eligible patient(s) have no propensity weight, and are left out of the betas.

", sep = "")   .bx <- .bx[!.no_w, , drop = FALSE] } # A response that does not vary cannot be associated with anything, and dividing by its SD would # fill every beta with NaN. Say so and let the betas read NA. .sd_y <- if (nrow(.bx) > 1L) stats::sd(.bx$log_rr) else NA_real_ .beta_fit <- is.finite(.sd_y) && .sd_y > 1e-8 if (!nrow(.bx)) {   cat(.no_elig_note, "

") } else if (!.beta_fit) {   cat("The estimated effect does not vary across patients, so no association can be estimated.

") } .bx$y <- if (.beta_fit) .bx$log_rr / .sd_y else rep(NA_real_, nrow(.bx)) # Each characteristic becomes ONE numeric column, fixed on the full sample before # any resampling: a number is standardized with the full-sample mean and SD; a # factor becomes 1 for its most common non-reference level, 0 for the reference # (its first level) and NA for every other level, so the regression compares # those two levels alone and drops the rest as missing. A resample then regresses on the same # column, so the coefficient means the same thing in every resample, and a # resample in which that column does not vary is unestimable: it gives NA and # is counted, never an error. .design <- lapply(.vt$predictors$names, function(v) {   xv <- .bx[[v]]   if (is.numeric(xv)) return(list(x = (xv - mean(xv, na.rm = TRUE)) / stats::sd(xv, na.rm = TRUE), label = v))   # The fit's own levels, kept even when no patient here carries one, so the   # column is the same whatever this sample happens to hold.   if (!is.factor(xv)) xv <- factor(xv)   ref <- levels(xv)[1L]   cnt <- table(xv)[levels(xv)[-1L]]   lev <- names(cnt)[order(-as.numeric(cnt), seq_along(cnt))][1L]   list(x = ifelse(xv == lev, 1, ifelse(xv == ref, 0, NA_real_)), label = paste0(v, ": ", lev, " vs ", ref)) }) .beta_one <- function(y, x, w) {   ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)   if (length(unique(x[ok])) < 2L) return(NA_real_)   unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(y[ok] ~ x[ok], weights = w[ok]))[2L]) } .betas <- data.frame(variable = vapply(.design, `[[`, "", "label"),                      beta = vapply(.design, function(z) .beta_one(.bx$y, z$x, .bx$w), numeric(1L)),                      lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_, unestimable = NA_integer_) if (BOOT > 0 && .beta_fit) {   set.seed(.vt$settings$seed)   .boot <- replicate(BOOT, {     i <- sample.int(nrow(.bx), replace = TRUE)     vapply(.design, function(z) .beta_one(.bx$y[i], z$x[i], .bx$w[i]), numeric(1L))   })   .boot <- matrix(.boot, nrow = length(.design))   .betas$lower <- apply(.boot, 1L, stats::quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)   .betas$upper <- apply(.boot, 1L, stats::quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)   .betas$unestimable <- rowSums(is.na(.boot)) } print(knitr::kable(.betas, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)) .bp <- .betas[is.finite(.betas$beta), ] if (!nrow(.bp)) {   cat("No beta could be estimated, so there is nothing to draw.
") } else {   .bp$variable <- factor(.bp$variable, levels = .bp$variable[order(.bp$beta)])   .fig <- ggplot(.bp, aes(x = beta, y = variable)) +     geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +     geom_point()   if (BOOT > 0) .fig <- .fig + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2, orientation = "y")   .fig <- .fig + labs(x = paste0("Standardized beta (positive: higher relative risk under ", ARMS[1], ")"), y = NULL)   save_figure(.fig, "vt-explain-betas")   .fig }

The cohort # above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other # patients are dropped and counted in the data table. #   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all. #   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record; list(rule = "first", by = "date") #     keeps one row per patient. This job models one row per #     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here. #   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key. JOIN <- NULL JOIN_VARS <- NULL REDUCE <- NULL JOIN_KEY <- NULL TIME <- "iv_reint" STATUS <- "reint" ARM <- "mv_procedure" # Demo: the two arms, in the order the difference is taken: a positive diff # favors ARMS[1]. ARMS <- c("repair", "replace") # Demo: rows that received neither arm are predicted under both and fit by # neither. NULL treats a missing ARM as no arm; a vector of levels names them. NO_ARM <- NULL # Demo: a vp-fit set ("<subject>-<type>") whose selected set the forests use, # or NULL to use PREDICTORS. The screen must not have seen the arm: that is what # makes it treatment-blind, and this job checks it. VP_SET <- NULL PREDICTORS <- c("age", "female", "bmi", "hx_chf", "hx_dm", "nyha_pr", "lvef", "creat_pr", "lvedd", "lvesd", "la_diam", "rvsp", "e_e") # Demo: anything measured after the treatment decision. A screen does not know # when a variable was measured, and a later procedure flag predicts the outcome # because it is part of the path to it. EXCLUDE <- character() # Demo: eligibility methods, one or more of "gower" and "sid". "sid" reads the # SID distance of the sid set named in SID_SET. ELIGIBILITY <- c("gower", "sid") COMBINE <- "any"                            # Demo: "any" flags a patient any method flags; "all" only when all do. SID_SET <- "echo-sid" # Demo: graded predictors coded as numbers (a 0 to 3 degree, say). The Gower # distance ranks them, so 0 against 3 is farther than 0 against 1; unnamed, every # mismatched grade counts the same. Names the predictors do not include are ignored. ORDINAL <- character() # Demo: "na.impute" imputes missing predictors inside each forest; "na.omit" # drops the patient. The outcome is required either way. NA_ACTION <- "na.impute" # Demo: for stacked multiple imputations, the column numbering them. This # release uses one completed dataset, IMPUTATION_USE; pooling is not done. IMPUTATION <- NULL IMPUTATION_USE <- 1L # Demo: the RMST horizon, in TIME's units. Keep it inside the follow-up of both # arms; past the last follow-up every curve is cut at the same place and the # difference means nothing. This job stops if it is not. HORIZON <- 8 NTREE <- 500 NSPLIT <- 8 SEED <- 1024                                # Demo: part of every cache key. # Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the # render instead of returning the old result; TRUE recomputes only the caches # that are out of date. REFIT <- FALSE  # Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher). # SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names # start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("vp-fit-coverage"). The names are the # file names, listed for each template in the templates README. SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE FIGURES <- NULL

It stops on a mismatch. hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml")) .cfg <- study_config(start = .root) # Stacked imputations repeat each patient once per imputation, so a row is unique on the ID and the imputation. if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) KEY <- unique(c(if (is.null(KEY)) ID else KEY, IMPUTATION)) job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,                                           where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,                                           reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY, one_row_per_patient = TRUE,                                           imputation = IMPUTATION) d <- job_data$data .provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),                       if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join)) knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", "")) if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) {   IMPUTATION <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$imputation   .m <- length(unique(d[[IMPUTATION]]))   if (!IMPUTATION_USE %in% d[[IMPUTATION]]) {     stop("IMPUTATION_USE = ", IMPUTATION_USE, " is not an imputation in ", IMPUTATION, ".", call. = FALSE)   }   d <- d[d[[IMPUTATION]] == IMPUTATION_USE, setdiff(names(d), IMPUTATION), drop = FALSE]   cat("This job uses imputation ", IMPUTATION_USE, " of ", .m, ". The forests are not pooled across imputations.\n",       sep = "") } # read_job_data() matches ID case-insensitively and falls back from ccfid to an # MRN, without changing ID here. Take the name it resolved. ID <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$id # This job saves one row per patient (vt.rds), and a sid set joins on it. No # saved artifact holds a raw identifier, an MRN least of all (#203), so the ID # is replaced here by its digest under the study's key, the form a sid set # saves too. Everything below, and everything saved, carries only the digest. .id_key <- hvtiRtemplates:::.study_id_key(.root) d[[ID]] <- hvtiRtemplates:::.id_digest(d[[ID]], .id_key) .no_arm <- if (is.null(NO_ARM)) is.na(d[[ARM]]) else d[[ARM]] %in% NO_ARM .treated <- d[[ARM]] %in% ARMS .other <- !.no_arm & !.treated if (any(.other)) {   stop(sum(.other), " row(s) have an ARM that is neither in ARMS nor NO_ARM: ",        paste(unique(d[[ARM]][.other]), collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE) } # Arms are names, never positions. A numeric ARM (0 and 1) would otherwise index # the lists of forests by position, so ARMS and the arm column become text once, # here, and every list below is keyed by that text. A missing arm stays NA. ARMS <- as.character(ARMS) d[[ARM]] <- as.character(d[[ARM]]) .no_outcome <- .treated & (is.na(d[[TIME]]) | is.na(d[[STATUS]])) if (any(.no_outcome)) {   stop(sum(.no_outcome), " treated patient(s) have no outcome. A forest cannot learn from them, and imputing one ",        "would invent follow-up. Resolve them in the dataset build.", call. = FALSE) } if (!all(d[[STATUS]][.treated] %in% c(0, 1))) stop(STATUS, " must be coded 0 and 1.", call. = FALSE) NA_ACTION <- match.arg(NA_ACTION, c("na.impute", "na.omit")) # Run again after na.omit drops patients (predictors chunk): the guard must hold for the patients the forests see. .arm_counts <- function(d, when = "") {   counts <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {     i <- d[[ARM]] %in% a     data.frame(Arm = a, Patients = sum(i), Events = sum(d[[STATUS]][i] == 1, na.rm = TRUE))   }))   thin <- counts$Patients < 2 | counts$Events < 1   if (any(thin)) {     stop("Each arm needs at least 2 treated patients and 1 event", when, "; ",          paste0(counts$Arm[thin], " has ", counts$Patients[thin], " patient(s) and ", counts$Events[thin], " event(s)",                 collapse = "; "), ".", call. = FALSE)   }   counts } .counts <- .arm_counts(d) .counts <- base::rbind(.counts, data.frame(Arm = "No arm", Patients = sum(.no_arm), Events = NA_integer_)) knitr::kable(.counts)

.vp_read <- NULL if (!is.null(VP_SET)) {   .vp_path <- file.path(dirname(dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))), VP_SET, "vp.rds")   if (!file.exists(.vp_path)) stop("No vp-fit screen at ", .vp_path, ". Render that job first.", call. = FALSE)   .vp_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.vp_path, "screen", .cfg, "the vp-fit job")   if (tolower(ARM) %in% tolower(.vp_read$value$coverage$variable)) {     stop("The screen in ", VP_SET, " was given ", ARM, " as a candidate, so it is not treatment-blind. ",          "Re-run vp-fit without the arm.", call. = FALSE)   }   .predictors <- .vp_read$value$selected   .provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, .vp_read$lineage$data) } else {   .predictors <- PREDICTORS } .predictors <- setdiff(.predictors, EXCLUDE) .leaks <- intersect(tolower(.predictors), tolower(c(ARM, TIME, STATUS, ID))) if (length(.leaks)) {   stop("PREDICTORS (or the screen) includes the arm, outcome or ID: ", paste(.leaks, collapse = ", "), ".",        call. = FALSE) } .missing <- setdiff(.predictors, names(d)) if (length(.missing)) stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE) if (!length(.predictors)) stop("No predictors are left after EXCLUDE.", call. = FALSE) .chr <- .predictors[vapply(d[.predictors], is.character, logical(1L))] d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor) if (NA_ACTION == "na.omit") {   .kept <- stats::complete.cases(d[.predictors])   cat(sum(!.kept), "patient(s) missing a predictor were dropped (NA_ACTION = \"na.omit\").\n")   d <- d[.kept, , drop = FALSE]   invisible(.arm_counts(d, " after NA_ACTION = \"na.omit\" dropped patients"))   .no_arm <- .no_arm[.kept]   .treated <- .treated[.kept] } d <- d[, c(ID, ARM, TIME, STATUS, .predictors), drop = FALSE] cat("Predictors:", paste(.predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n") Predictors: age, female, bmi, hx_chf, hx_dm, nyha_pr, lvef, creat_pr, lvedd, lvesd, la_diam, rvsp, e_e
