# One rule, applied to any patient-by-patient distance. For each arm, each # patient's nearest neighbor in that arm (never themself) is compared with the # largest nearest-neighbor distance among the arm's own patients. Farther than # that, STRICTLY, and the arm's forest would be extrapolating. A treated patient # is judged against the other arm; a row with no arm against both. # # A distance can be unavailable: Gower gives NA for two patients who share no # observed predictor. An unavailable distance is no evidence of nearness, so it # counts as infinitely far. A patient with no finite distance to any patient in # an arm has no comparable neighbor there and is out of distribution for it, # with that reason; an arm member with no finite within-arm neighbor does not # set the arm's reference. Every judged patient therefore gets TRUE or FALSE, # never NA. vt_ood <- function(dist, ids, arm, arms) {   dist <- as.matrix(dist)[ids, ids, drop = FALSE]   dist[is.na(dist)] <- Inf   diag(dist) <- Inf   rows <- lapply(arms, function(a) {     members <- which(arm %in% a)     nn_within <- apply(dist[members, members, drop = FALSE], 1L, min)     nn_within <- nn_within[is.finite(nn_within)]     # An arm whose members have no finite neighbor has no reference gap, so nobody can be shown     # to sit inside it: they are flagged with that reason, and the eligibility chunk stops on it.     reference <- if (length(nn_within)) max(nn_within) else NA_real_     judged <- which(is.na(arm) | !arm %in% c(a, NA))     if (!length(judged)) return(NULL)     sub <- dist[judged, members, drop = FALSE]     nn <- apply(sub, 1L, which.min)     distance <- sub[cbind(seq_along(judged), nn)]     none <- !is.finite(distance)     out <- none | is.na(reference) | distance > reference     reason <- ifelse(none, sprintf("no comparable %s patient (no predictor observed in common)", a), "")     if (is.na(reference)) {       reason[!none] <- sprintf("arm %s has no reference gap", a)     } else {       reason[out & !none] <- sprintf("nearest %s patient at %.3f, beyond that arm's largest gap %.3f",                                      a, distance[out & !none], reference)     }     data.frame(ID = ids[judged], method = NA_character_, arm = a, nn_id = ifelse(none, NA, ids[members][nn]),                distance = distance, reference = reference,                ratio = if (length(nn_within)) distance / stats::median(nn_within) else NA_real_,                in_distribution = !out, reason = reason)   })   do.call(base::rbind, rows) }  # Gower over the model predictors only: mixed types, no model, bounded in [0, 1]. # A 0/1 column is declared symmetric binary. daisy() would otherwise treat it as # interval scaled, which gives the same distance, and warn in every report. # daisy() scores any mismatch of an unordered factor as 1, so a grade of 0 # against 3 would count the same as 0 against 1. The `ordinal` predictors become # ordered factors, levels sorted by their numeric codes, which daisy ranks and # scales to [0, 1]. Only the distance sees this; the forests keep the data as read. vt_elig_gower <- function(d, predictors, id, ordinal = character()) {   x <- d[predictors]   for (v in intersect(ordinal, predictors)) {     lv <- levels(factor(x[[v]]))     num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(lv))     if (anyNA(num)) {       stop("ORDINAL predictor ", v, " has levels that are not numeric codes: ", paste(lv[is.na(num)], collapse = ", "),            ".", call. = FALSE)     }     x[[v]] <- factor(as.character(x[[v]]), levels = lv[order(num)], ordered = TRUE)   }   binary <- predictors[vapply(x, function(col) {     col <- stats::na.omit(col)     is.numeric(col) && length(unique(col)) == 2L && all(col %in% c(0, 1))   }, logical(1L))]   m <- as.matrix(cluster::daisy(x, metric = "gower", type = if (length(binary)) list(symm = binary) else list()))   dimnames(m) <- list(d[[id]], d[[id]])   m }  # Which predictors put an out-of-distribution patient outside the arm they were # judged against: a number outside the range the arm's patients span, or a level # that at most `rare` of them share. A distance says how far; this says why, in # terms a clinician can check against the chart. At most `n` are named; a patient # with none is unusual only in combination. vt_ood_features <- function(out_rows, d, id, arm_of, predictors, n = 3L, rare = 2L) {   vapply(seq_len(nrow(out_rows)), function(i) {     p <- d[match(out_rows$ID[i], d[[id]]), , drop = FALSE]     members <- d[arm_of %in% out_rows$arm[i], , drop = FALSE]     why <- character()     for (v in predictors) {       a <- p[[v]]       u <- members[[v]]       if (is.na(a)) next       if (is.numeric(u) && !all(stats::na.omit(u) %in% c(0, 1))) {         rg <- range(u, na.rm = TRUE)         if (a < rg[1] || a > rg[2]) {           why <- c(why, sprintf("%s %s outside %s's range [%s, %s]", v, format(signif(a, 3)), out_rows$arm[i],                                 format(signif(rg[1], 3)), format(signif(rg[2], 3))))         }       } else {         k <- sum(as.character(u) == as.character(a), na.rm = TRUE)         if (k <= rare) why <- c(why, sprintf("%s = %s (%d of %d in %s)", v, as.character(a), k, nrow(members), out_rows$arm[i]))       }     }     if (!length(why)) "none alone; unusual in combination" else paste(utils::head(why, n), collapse = "; ")   }, character(1L)) }  # The SID distance a sid job saved. Read, never refit, and refused when it does # not cover every patient here. # Returns the distance with the whole reader result as attribute "read", so the # eligibility chunk can carry the sid set's record and lineage into vt.rds. vt_elig_sid <- function(path, ids, cfg, key = NULL,                         read = function(p) hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(p, "SID fit", cfg, "the sid job")) {   if (!file.exists(path)) stop("No sid clustering at ", path, ". Render that job first.", call. = FALSE)   got <- read(path)   # A sid set's distance is labeled by ID digests under the study key, with the   # key's fingerprint saved beside it. A different fingerprint means the key   # changed since, and every digest would miss.   if (!is.null(key) && !identical(got$value$id_key, hvtiRtemplates:::.id_key_fingerprint(key))) {     stop("The sid set at ", path, " was digested under a different study key. Re-render it.", call. = FALSE)   }   m <- as.matrix(got$value$dist)   absent <- setdiff(ids, rownames(m))   if (length(absent)) {     stop(length(absent), " patient(s) in this job are not in the sid distance at ", path, ".", call. = FALSE)   }   structure(m[ids, ids, drop = FALSE], read = got) }  # A patient is eligible when every arm they were judged against passed, per # method; then methods combine: "any" flag excludes, or "all" must. vt_combine <- function(rows, combine = c("any", "all")) {   combine <- match.arg(combine)   per <- stats::aggregate(in_distribution ~ ID + method, rows, all)   flagged <- stats::aggregate(!in_distribution ~ ID, per, if (combine == "any") any else all)   data.frame(ID = flagged$ID, elig = !flagged[[2]]) } .methods <- match.arg(ELIGIBILITY, c("gower", "sid"), several.ok = TRUE) .ids <- d[[ID]] .arm <- ifelse(.no_arm, NA_character_, as.character(d[[ARM]])) .sid_read <- NULL .dist <- list(   gower = function() vt_elig_gower(d, .predictors, ID, ORDINAL),   sid = function() {     if (is.null(SID_SET)) stop("ELIGIBILITY includes "sid"; name the sid set in SID_SET.", call. = FALSE)     m <- vt_elig_sid(file.path(dirname(dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))), SID_SET, "sid.rds"), .ids, .cfg,                      key = .id_key)     # The sid set decided some flags, so its record and data lineage travel     # into vt.rds with the vp screen's (see `save`).     .sid_read <<- attr(m, "read")     .provenance_data <<- c(.provenance_data, .sid_read$lineage$data)     m   } ) .elig_rows <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(.methods, function(m) transform(vt_ood(.dist[[m]](), .ids, .arm, ARMS), method = m))) if (anyNA(.elig_rows$reference)) {   .bad <- unique(.elig_rows$method[is.na(.elig_rows$reference)])   stop("An arm has no two patients with a finite distance by ", paste(.bad, collapse = ", "),        ", so its reference gap is undefined. Check the predictors' missingness.", call. = FALSE) } .elig_rows$features <- "" .ood_at <- which(!.elig_rows$in_distribution) .elig_rows$features[.ood_at] <- vt_ood_features(.elig_rows[.ood_at, ], d, ID, .arm, .predictors) # With no finite distance there is no comparison to explain; vt_ood()'s reason says why. .nofin <- .ood_at[!is.finite(.elig_rows$distance[.ood_at])] .elig_rows$features[.nofin] <- .elig_rows$reason[.nofin] .elig <- vt_combine(.elig_rows, COMBINE) for (m in .methods) {   .one <- vt_combine(.elig_rows[.elig_rows$method == m, ], "any")   .elig[[paste0("elig_", m)]] <- .one$elig[match(.elig$ID, .one$ID)] } # Sensitivity only, never part of the combined rule: forest propensity common support. # ps_forest() refuses missing predictors, while the arm forests impute them # (NA_ACTION = "na.impute"). So the propensity model gets a forest-imputed copy # of the treated patients' predictors, seeded, and the arm forests keep the # data as read. The arm is left out of the imputation, so the treatment does not # shape the predictors that then predict it. Under "na.omit" nothing is missing and the copy equals d. .ps_data <- d[.treated, c(ID, ARM, .predictors), drop = FALSE] if (anyNA(.ps_data[.predictors])) {   .imp <- .ps_data[.predictors]   # impute() drops a patient who is missing every predictor, so the imputed   # rows are matched back by ID (its row names), never by position.   rownames(.imp) <- .ps_data[[ID]]   set.seed(SEED)   .imputed <- randomForestSRC::impute(data = .imp, ntree = 100L, seed = -abs(SEED), verbose = FALSE)   .back <- match(.ps_data[[ID]], rownames(.imputed))   if (anyNA(.back)) {     cat(sum(is.na(.back)), " treated patient(s) could not be scored for the propensity sensitivity ",         "(no predictor observed); they are not eligible under it.
", sep = "")   }   .ps_data <- .ps_data[!is.na(.back), , drop = FALSE]   .ps_data[.predictors] <- .imputed[.back[!is.na(.back)], .predictors, drop = FALSE] } set.seed(SEED) # The propensity forest keeps its formula too, and reformulate() would tie it to this # environment (and the raw IDs in `job_data`); point it at the global environment. .ps_model <- stats::reformulate(.predictors, ARM, env = globalenv()) .ps <- ps_forest(.ps_model, data = .ps_data, treatment_col = ARM, id_col = ID,                  treated_level = ARMS[1], ntree = NTREE, seed = -abs(SEED)) # ps_support() adds weak_common (outside the range both arms occupy) to $data. # Patients with no arm have no propensity score and are not judged by it. .support <- ps_support(.ps)$data .elig$elig_propensity <- .elig$ID %in% .support[[ID]][!.support$weak_common] .elig$elig_none <- TRUE .out <- .elig_rows[!.elig_rows$in_distribution, c("ID", "method", "arm", "distance", "reference", "features")] if (nrow(.out)) {   .out$distance <- round(.out$distance, 3)   .out$reference <- round(.out$reference, 3) } cat(nrow(.out), "patient-by-arm judgments are out of distribution; every one is listed.
") 0 patient-by-arm judgments are out of distribution; every one is listed. knitr::kable(.out, row.names = FALSE) .plot <- .elig_rows[is.finite(.elig_rows$distance), ] .plot <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(split(.plot, list(.plot$method, .plot$arm), drop = TRUE), function(x) {   x$rank <- rank(x$distance, ties.method = "first")   x })) .ref <- unique(.plot[c("method", "arm", "reference")]) .fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(.plot, ggplot2::aes(x = rank, y = distance, color = in_distribution)) +   ggplot2::geom_point() +   ggplot2::geom_hline(data = .ref, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = reference), linetype = "dashed") +   ggplot2::facet_grid(method ~ arm, scales = "free") +   ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "gray60", `FALSE` = "black")) +   ggplot2::labs(x = "Patient rank", y = "Distance to nearest patient in the arm", color = "In distribution") +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-eligibility") .fig if (length(.methods) > 1L) {   .pairs <- utils::combn(.methods, 2L, simplify = FALSE)   for (.p in .pairs) {     cat("Eligible under", .p[1], "(rows) and", .p[2], "(columns):

CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds")) .model <- stats::as.formula(paste0("Surv(", TIME, ", ", STATUS, ") ~ ", paste(.predictors, collapse = " + "))) # The saved forest keeps this formula, and a formula keeps the environment it # was made in, `job_data` and its patient IDs included. Point it at the global # environment, which a saved file only refers to (rfs-fit does the same). environment(.model) <- globalenv() # The IDs of each forest's training rows, in training order. survival.oob rows # follow this order, and vt_curves() matches on it rather than on d's order. .train_ids <- stats::setNames(lapply(ARMS, function(a) d[[ID]][d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated]), ARMS) .forests <- stats::setNames(lapply(ARMS, function(a) {   da <- d[d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated, c(TIME, STATUS, .predictors), drop = FALSE]   set.seed(SEED)   cache_fit(paste0("vt-fit-", a),             rfsrc(.model, data = da, ntree = NTREE, nsplit = NSPLIT, na.action = NA_ACTION,                   importance = "none", block.size = 1, seed = -abs(SEED)),             seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT) }), ARMS) .perf <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {   f <- .forests[[a]]   # yvar is the response as a data frame (time, status) for a survival forest.   yt <- f$yvar[[1]]   ys <- f$yvar[[2]]   cc <- survival::concordance(survival::Surv(yt, ys) ~ f$predicted.oob, reverse = TRUE)   se <- sqrt(cc$var)   data.frame(arm = a, patients = f$n, events = sum(ys == 1), c_index = cc$concordance,              lower = cc$concordance - 1.96 * se, upper = cc$concordance + 1.96 * se) })) cat(knitr::kable(.perf, digits = 3), sep = "
") .weak <- .perf$arm[which(.perf$lower <= 0.5)] if (length(.weak)) {   cat("
**The interval for", paste(.weak, collapse = " and "), "includes 0.5.** That arm's half of every",       "contrast below is exploratory.
") } # Out-of-bag predicted survival at the horizon against Kaplan-Meier within # groups of predicted survival, for one survival forest. survival.oob and yvar # share the training order, so no matching by ID is needed. A patient never out # of bag has no prediction and is left out, counted. A group whose follow-up # ends before the horizon has no observed survival there: extending its curve # would treat the last censored patients as immortal. It is NA, counted, unless # the curve had already reached zero. vt_calibration <- function(f, horizon, groups = 5L) {   at <- findInterval(horizon, f$time.interest)   pred <- if (at == 0L) rep(1, f$n) else f$survival.oob[, at]   time <- f$yvar[[1]]   status <- f$yvar[[2]]   ok <- !is.na(pred)   pred <- pred[ok]   time <- time[ok]   status <- status[ok]   breaks <- unique(stats::quantile(pred, seq(0, 1, length.out = groups + 1L), names = FALSE))   g <- if (length(breaks) > 1L) cut(pred, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) else rep(1L, length(pred))   out <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(sort(unique(g)), function(k) {     s <- g == k     km <- summary(survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time[s], status[s]) ~ 1), times = horizon, extend = TRUE)     observed <- if (length(km$surv)) km$surv else NA_real_     if (max(time[s]) < horizon && !isTRUE(observed == 0)) observed <- NA_real_     data.frame(group = k, patients = sum(s), events = sum(status[s] == 1), predicted = mean(pred[s]),                observed = observed)   }))   attr(out, "no_prediction") <- sum(!ok)   attr(out, "unsupported") <- sum(is.na(out$observed))   out } .cal <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {   x <- vt_calibration(.forests[[a]], HORIZON)   if (attr(x, "no_prediction")) {     cat(attr(x, "no_prediction"), " ", a, " patient(s) were never out of bag and have no calibration prediction; ",         "raise NTREE.

", sep = "")   }   if (attr(x, "unsupported")) {     cat(attr(x, "unsupported"), " ", a, " fifth(s) have no follow-up to ", HORIZON,         " and no observed survival there; they are left out of the error.

", sep = "")   }   cbind(arm = a, x) })) cat(knitr::kable(.cal, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE), sep = "
") # One number per arm: the mean distance between predicted and observed over the fifths, in percentage points. .cal_error <- tapply(abs(.cal$predicted - .cal$observed), .cal$arm, mean, na.rm = TRUE)[ARMS] cat("
Mean calibration error at ", HORIZON, ", in percentage points: ",     paste0(ARMS, " ", format(round(100 * .cal_error, 1), nsmall = 1), collapse = ", "), ".
", sep = "") .lim <- range(c(.cal$predicted, .cal$observed), na.rm = TRUE) .fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(.cal[!is.na(.cal$observed), , drop = FALSE], ggplot2::aes(x = predicted, y = observed)) +   ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ arm) +   ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = .lim, ylim = .lim) +   ggplot2::labs(x = paste("Predicted survival at", HORIZON, "(out of bag)"), y = "Observed, Kaplan-Meier") +   hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-calibration") .fig

# Two curves per patient. The arm a patient received comes from that arm's # forest OUT OF BAG, so no one is predicted by trees grown on them. The other # arm comes from predict() on the other forest. Rows with no arm get both from # predict(). Everything is keyed by ID: predict() returns rows in the order it # was given them, and pairing by position silently swaps patients. Under # na.impute predict() imputes the new rows at random, so it takes the seed too. vt_curves <- function(forests, train_ids, d, id, arm, arms, no_arm, seed) {   out <- list()   for (a in arms) {     f <- forests[[a]]     own <- d[[arm]] %in% a & !no_arm     own_ids <- d[[id]][own]     # survival.oob rows are in TRAINING order, which train_ids records; d may     # be in any order, so each own-arm patient is matched to their row by ID.     at <- match(own_ids, train_ids[[a]])     if (anyNA(at)) stop(sum(is.na(at)), " arm ", a, " patient(s) are not among its forest's training rows.", call. = FALSE)     oob <- f$survival.oob[at, , drop = FALSE]     out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(ID = rep(own_ids, each = length(f$time.interest)), arm_of_curve = a,                                           time = f$time.interest, surv = as.vector(t(oob)))     other <- d[!own, , drop = FALSE]     p <- predict(f, newdata = other[, f$xvar.names, drop = FALSE], na.action = "na.impute",                  seed = seed)     out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(ID = rep(other[[id]], each = length(f$time.interest)), arm_of_curve = a,                                           time = f$time.interest, surv = as.vector(t(p$survival)))   }   do.call(base::rbind, out) } .own_n <- vapply(ARMS, function(a) .forests[[a]]$n, integer(1L)) stopifnot(all(.own_n == lengths(.train_ids[ARMS]))) set.seed(SEED) .curves <- vt_curves(.forests, .train_ids, d, ID, ARM, ARMS, no_arm = .no_arm, seed = -abs(SEED))

code: # RMST to the horizon: the area under a step survival curve, which starts at 1. # The horizon must sit inside both arms' follow-up; past it every curve is cut # at the same place and the difference is an artifact (a horizon in days on a # fit in years gave identical curves once). vt_rmst <- function(curves, horizon, arms, followup) {   past <- names(followup)[followup < horizon]   if (length(past)) {     stop("HORIZON (", horizon, ") is beyond the largest follow-up time in arm(s) ", paste(past, collapse = ", "),          " (", paste(signif(followup[past], 3), collapse = ", "), "). Check its units against TIME.", call. = FALSE)   }   # The risk is 1 - S(horizon), where S includes a step AT the horizon; the   # area stops at the horizon, so a step there adds nothing to it.   one <- function(t, s) {     keep <- t < horizon     knots <- c(0, t[keep], horizon)     steps <- c(1, s[keep])     at <- c(1, s[t <= horizon])     c(rmst = sum(diff(knots) * steps), risk = 1 - utils::tail(at, 1L))   }   per <- lapply(split(curves, list(curves$ID, curves$arm_of_curve), drop = TRUE), function(x) {     x <- x[order(x$time), ]     v <- one(x$time, x$surv)     data.frame(ID = x$ID[1L], arm_of_curve = x$arm_of_curve[1L], rmst = v[["rmst"]], risk = v[["risk"]])   })   long <- do.call(base::rbind, per)   wide <- stats::reshape(long, idvar = "ID", timevar = "arm_of_curve", direction = "wide", sep = "_")   wide$diff <- wide[[paste0("rmst_", arms[1])]] - wide[[paste0("rmst_", arms[2])]]   # log_rr is +/-Inf or NaN when a patient's risk is 0 under an arm (vt-explain drops and counts those).   wide$log_rr <- log(wide[[paste0("risk_", arms[1])]] / wide[[paste0("risk_", arms[2])]])   rownames(wide) <- NULL   wide } .followup <- vapply(ARMS, function(a) max(d[[TIME]][d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated]), numeric(1L)) .rmst <- vt_rmst(.curves, HORIZON, ARMS, .followup) # no_arm marks the patients who received neither arm. Their arm is NA, never a label, so # an arm that is really named "none" cannot be confused with them. .rmst <- merge(data.frame(ID = d[[ID]], arm = ifelse(.no_arm, NA_character_, d[[ARM]]), no_arm = .no_arm),                .rmst, by = "ID") .rmst <- merge(.rmst, .elig, by = "ID") .in_dist <- .rmst$ID[.rmst$elig] if (!length(.in_dist)) {   cat("No patient is in distribution under the combined rule; see the eligibility tables.\n") } else {   .mc <- .curves[.curves$ID %in% .in_dist, ]   .at <- match(.mc$ID, .rmst$ID)   .mc$received <- ifelse(.rmst$no_arm[.at], "No arm", .rmst$arm[.at])   .mc <- stats::aggregate(surv ~ received + arm_of_curve + time, data = .mc, FUN = mean)   # hv_rmst_curves() wants right-continuous steps that start at time 0 with surv 1.   .mc <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(split(.mc, list(.mc$received, .mc$arm_of_curve), drop = TRUE), function(x) {     base::rbind(data.frame(received = x$received[1L], arm_of_curve = x$arm_of_curve[1L], time = 0, surv = 1), x[order(x$time), ])   }))   .mc$facet <- paste("Received", .mc$received)   .mc$arm <- .mc$arm_of_curve   .fig <- plot(hvtiPlotR::hv_rmst_curves(.mc, tau = HORIZON, facet = "facet", arm = "arm")) +     ggplot2::labs(x = "Time", y = "Mean predicted survival", color = "Curve under", fill = "Curve under")   save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-curves")   .fig }

# The product of this job, and what vt-explain reads, in one file so its parts # cannot drift apart. The forests are kept so vt-explain grows none. vt_handoff <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(   list(rmst = .rmst, curves = .curves, forests = .forests,        eligibility = list(rows = .elig_rows, methods = .methods, combine = COMBINE, sid_set = SID_SET, ordinal = ORDINAL,                           ps = .ps),        predictors = list(names = .predictors, vp_set = VP_SET),        settings = list(performance = .perf, calibration = .cal, arms = ARMS, horizon = HORIZON, ntree = NTREE, seed = SEED,                        time = TIME, status = STATUS,                        id = ID, id_key = hvtiRtemplates:::.id_key_fingerprint(.id_key),                        arm = ARM, imputation = IMPUTATION, imputation_use = IMPUTATION_USE,                        imputation_m = if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) .m,                        # Everything read_job_data() was given, so vt-explain reads the same patients and values.                        read = list(dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET, where = WHERE, key = KEY,                                    join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS, reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY))),   # .provenance_data already holds the vp and sid sets' data lineage (appended   # where each was read); their handoff records go in as artifacts.   data = .provenance_data,   artifacts = c(list(), if (!is.null(.vp_read)) c(.vp_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.vp_read$record)),                 if (!is.null(.sid_read)) c(.sid_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.sid_read$record))),   analysis = list(time = list(variable = TIME), event = list(variable = STATUS, event = 1L, censored = 0L)),   selection = attr(job_data$record, "selection") ) saveRDS(vt_handoff, set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))

code: # \donttest{ root <- file.path(tempdir(), "upgrade-job-example") invisible(hvtiRutilities::study_setup(root, "Example", 1L, renv = FALSE)) job <- add_job("dc", "cohort", "eda", dir = root, qualifier = "general") # A study choice, made in the job. lines <- readLines(job) lines <- sub('^DATASET <- "built"', 'DATASET <- "built_r"', lines) writeLines(lines, job) upgraded <- upgrade_job(job) grep("^DATASET <- ", readLines(upgraded), value = TRUE) #> [1] "DATASET <- \"built_r\"" unlink(root, recursive = TRUE) # }
